Overlapping src and dst is unspecified here; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.
Pointers must be non-null; behavior is undefined otherwise.

functions.name: camellia192_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: void camellia192_set_encrypt_key(struct camellia256_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Camellia-192 key schedule in ctx for encryption. Uses the same context type as Camellia-256, but with the 192-bit key schedule. Expands a 24-byte key for encryption.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct camellia256_ctx (camellia192_ctx is defined as camellia256_ctx).
key must point to exactly 24 bytes (CAMELLIA192_KEY_SIZE) of key material.
ctx must be initialized by this function (or camellia192_set_decrypt_key/camellia256_invert_key via alias) before passing it to camellia256_crypt/camellia192_crypt.
Pointers must be non-null; behavior is undefined otherwise.

functions.name: camellia192_set_decrypt_key

functions.description: Initializes a Camellia-192 key schedule in ctx for decryption. Uses the same context type as Camellia-256, but with the 192-bit key schedule. Expands a 24-byte key for decryption.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct camellia256_ctx (camellia192_ctx is defined as camellia256_ctx).
key must point to exactly 24 bytes (CAMELLIA192_KEY_SIZE) of key material.
ctx must be initialized by this function (or camellia192_set_encrypt_key/camellia256_invert_key via alias) before passing it to camellia256_crypt/camellia192_crypt.
Pointers must be non-null; behavior is undefined otherwise.

functions.name: camellia192_invert_key
functions.signature: void camellia192_invert_key(struct camellia256_ctx *dst, const struct camellia256_ctx *src);
functions.description: Builds the inverse key schedule in dst from an existing Camellia-192 key schedule in src. This is a macro alias for camellia256_invert_key but logically inverts a 192-bit schedule.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct camellia256_ctx (camellia192_ctx).
src must be a valid pointer to a previously initialized Camellia-192 context created by camellia192_set_encrypt_key or camellia192_set_decrypt_key.
In-place inversion (dst == src) is unknown from this header and should be avoided unless documented elsewhere.
Pointers must be non-null; behavior is undefined otherwise.

functions.name: camellia192_crypt
functions.signature: void camellia192_crypt(const struct camellia256_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts data using Camellia-192 in ECB-like block processing, according to the direction encoded in ctx. This is a macro alias to camellia256_crypt, operating on a ctx initialized for 192-bit keys.
requirements: ctx must point to a struct camellia256_ctx initialized by camellia192_set_encrypt_key (for encryption) or camellia192_set_decrypt_key/camellia192_invert_key (for decryption).
length must be a multiple of CAMELLIA_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes; partial blocks are not supported by this function.
dst must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.

Overlapping src and dst is unspecified here; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.

functions.name: cbc_encrypt
functions.signature: void cbc_encrypt(const void *ctx, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t block_size, uint8_t *iv, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts data using Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with a caller-supplied block cipher function. The cipher context and function pointer define the underlying block cipher. The IV is used for the first block and is updated in place to the last produced ciphertext block. No padding is performed; callers must supply data in whole blocks. Typical use: initialize the cipher context and IV, then call to encrypt a buffer whose length is a multiple of the block size.
requirements: ctx must point to an initialized cipher context suitable for encryption with function f.
f must be a valid block cipher encryption function compatible with ctx and having the given block_size (type: nettle_cipher_func).
block_size must be the block size of the underlying cipher (> 0).
iv must point to at least block_size bytes; it will be read and updated in place to the last ciphertext block.
length must be a multiple of block_size; no padding is applied by this function.
dst must point to a buffer of at least length bytes for output.
src must point to a buffer of at least length bytes of input plaintext.
This function returns void and does not report errors; callers must ensure all preconditions (sizes, initialization) are satisfied.
In-place encryption (dst == src) is not documented here; behavior is unknown without further library documentation.

functions.name: cbc_decrypt
functions.signature: void cbc_decrypt(const void *ctx, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t block_size, uint8_t *iv, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts data using Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with a caller-supplied block cipher function. The cipher context and function pointer define the underlying block cipher. IV is used for the first block and updated in place to the last processed ciphertext block. No padding is removed; callers must provide data in whole blocks and handle padding externally if used.
requirements: ctx must point to an initialized cipher context suitable for decryption with function f.
f must be a valid block cipher decryption function compatible with ctx and having the given block_size (type: nettle_cipher_func).
block_size must be the block size of the underlying cipher (> 0).
iv must point to at least block_size bytes; it will be read and updated in place to the last ciphertext block of src.
length must be a multiple of block_size; no padding handling is performed.
dst must point to a buffer of at least length bytes for output plaintext.
src must point to a buffer of at least length bytes of input ciphertext.
This function returns void; callers must ensure preconditions are satisfied.
In-place decryption (dst == src) is not documented here; behavior is unknown without further library documentation.

functions.name: cbc_aes128_encrypt
functions.signature: void cbc_aes128_encrypt(const struct aes128_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *iv, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts data using AES-128 in CBC mode. Uses the supplied AES-128 context and IV; the IV is updated in place to the last ciphertext block. No padding is performed; data length must be a multiple of 16 bytes.
requirements: ctx must point to an initialized AES-128 encryption context (e.g., set via aes128_set_encrypt_key).
iv must point to at least 16 bytes; it is read and updated in place to the last ciphertext block.
length must be a multiple of 16 bytes; no padding is applied.
dst must point to a buffer of at least length bytes for ciphertext output.
src must point to a buffer of at least length bytes for plaintext input.
This function returns void; callers must ensure input sizes and initialization are correct.
In-place operation (dst == src) is not documented here; behavior is unknown without further library documentation.

functions.name: cbc_aes192_encrypt
functions.signature: void cbc_aes192_encrypt(const struct aes192_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *iv, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts data using AES-192 in CBC mode. Uses the supplied AES-192 context and IV; the IV is updated in place to the last ciphertext block. No padding is performed; data length must be a multiple of 16 bytes.

functions.signature: void cbc_aes256_encrypt(const struct aes256_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *iv, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts data using AES-256 in CBC mode. Uses the supplied AES-256 context and IV; the IV is updated in place to the last ciphertext block. No padding is performed; data length must be a multiple of 16 bytes.
requirements: ctx must point to an initialized AES-256 encryption context (e.g., set via aes256_set_encrypt_key).
iv must point to at least 16 bytes; it is read and updated in place to the last ciphertext block.
length must be a multiple of 16 bytes; no padding is applied.

This function returns void; callers must ensure input sizes and initialization are correct.

functions.name: ccm_set_nonce
functions.signature: void ccm_set_nonce(struct ccm_ctx *ctx, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t noncelen, const uint8_t *nonce, size_t authlen, size_t msglen, size_t taglen);
functions.description: Initializes per-message CCM state with nonce, lengths, and tag size, preparing the context for processing associated data and payload using the provided block cipher (128-bit block) via the given Nettle cipher function pointer. Must be called before ccm_update/ccm_encrypt/ccm_decrypt/ccm_digest for each message.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable CCM context.
cipher must point to a valid, initialized block cipher context compatible with f (128-bit block, e.g., AES).
f must be a valid Nettle block cipher function for CTR/CBC-MAC use with the provided cipher context.
noncelen must be between CCM_MIN_NONCE_SIZE (7) and CCM_MAX_NONCE_SIZE (14), inclusive.
nonce must point to noncelen bytes.
authlen is the total length in bytes of the associated data to be processed via ccm_update; it must reflect the actual total AAD length that will be supplied.
msglen is the total plaintext/ciphertext payload length in bytes that will be processed via ccm_encrypt/ccm_decrypt; it must reflect the actual total payload length.
msglen must be ≤ CCM_MAX_MSG_SIZE(noncelen).

taglen is the requested authentication tag length in bytes (must match the length later passed to ccm_digest). Exact permitted values are not specified here; use values accepted by the implementation (commonly 4..16 even lengths).
Must be called once per message prior to any ccm_update/ccm_encrypt/ccm_decrypt/ccm_digest calls for that message.
Streaming is not supported for sizing; the total AAD and message lengths must be known up front as provided here.

functions.name: ccm_update
functions.signature: void ccm_update(struct ccm_ctx *ctx, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds associated data (AAD) into the CCM CBC-MAC using the given block cipher function and context. Does not produce output; used to authenticate but not encrypt AAD.
requirements: ccm_set_nonce must have been called on ctx for the current message.
cipher and f must match those used in ccm_set_nonce for this message.
data must point to length bytes; length may be zero.
The total number of bytes passed across all ccm_update calls must equal the authlen value provided to ccm_set_nonce.
ctx must remain valid and unmodified by the caller across calls.

functions.name: ccm_encrypt
functions.signature: void ccm_encrypt(struct ccm_ctx *ctx, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts plaintext payload using CCM’s CTR mode while updating the CBC-MAC for authentication. Writes ciphertext to dst.
requirements: ccm_set_nonce must have been called on ctx for the current message.
cipher and f must match those used in ccm_set_nonce for this message.
src must point to length bytes of plaintext; dst must point to a buffer of at least length bytes.
The total number of bytes processed across ccm_encrypt/ccm_decrypt for the message must equal the msglen supplied to ccm_set_nonce.
dst and src must be valid for reading/writing the specified length; in-place behavior is not specified.
length may be zero.

functions.signature: void ccm_decrypt(struct ccm_ctx *ctx, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts ciphertext payload using CCM’s CTR mode while updating the CBC-MAC for authentication. Writes plaintext to dst. Tag verification is not done here; use ccm_digest to compute/compare the tag.
requirements: ccm_set_nonce must have been called on ctx for the current message.
cipher and f must match those used in ccm_set_nonce for this message.
src must point to length bytes of ciphertext; dst must point to a buffer of at least length bytes.
The total number of bytes processed across ccm_encrypt/ccm_decrypt for the message must equal the msglen supplied to ccm_set_nonce.
dst and src must be valid for reading/writing the specified length; in-place behavior is not specified.
length may be zero.

functions.signature: void ccm_digest(struct ccm_ctx *ctx, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes and outputs the CCM authentication tag (MAC) of the specified length for the current message using the given cipher. Typically called after all AAD and payload have been processed via ccm_update and ccm_encrypt/decrypt.
requirements: ccm_set_nonce must have been called on ctx for the current message.
cipher and f must match those used in ccm_set_nonce for this message.

All AAD (authlen bytes total) must have been supplied via ccm_update, and all payload (msglen bytes total) via ccm_encrypt/ccm_decrypt, before calling.

requirements: cipher must point to a valid, initialized 128-bit block cipher context compatible with f.
f must be a valid Nettle block cipher function pointer for the provided cipher.
nlength (nonce length) must be between CCM_MIN_NONCE_SIZE (7) and CCM_MAX_NONCE_SIZE (14), inclusive.
nonce must point to nlength bytes.
adata must point to alength bytes of associated data (alength may be zero).
tlength is the desired tag length in bytes; exact allowed set is not specified here and must be acceptable to the implementation.
src must point to clength - tlength bytes of plaintext.
dst must point to a buffer of at least clength bytes to receive ciphertext followed by the tag.
clength must equal mlength + tlength, where mlength is the plaintext size; per comment: clength = sizeof(ciphertext) = mlength + tlength.
The plaintext size mlength must be ≤ CCM_MAX_MSG_SIZE(nlength).

requirements: q must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage of at least CURVE25519_SIZE (32) bytes.
n must be a non-NULL pointer to readable storage of at least CURVE25519_SIZE (32) bytes.
p must be a non-NULL pointer to readable storage of at least CURVE25519_SIZE (32) bytes, containing the 32-byte u-coordinate (public key) as defined by RFC 7748 (X25519).

Per RFC 7748 conformance (NETTLE_CURVE25519_RFC7748 == 1), inputs n and p are 32-byte strings; the operation is defined for any 32-byte p, and scalar handling follows RFC 7748 semantics (e.g., internal clamping).
The function returns void; callers must not expect error codes or exceptions and must use q to obtain the result.
Thread-safety and buffer aliasing (whether q may alias n or p) are not specified; callers should avoid overlapping buffers unless documentation elsewhere guarantees it.

functions.name: curve448_mul_g
functions.signature: void curve448_mul_g(uint8_t *q, const uint8_t *n);
functions.description: Computes a Curve448/X448 scalar multiplication of the canonical base point (generator) by the scalar n, writing the 56-byte u-coordinate result to q. Typical usage: derive a public key from a 56-byte private scalar for X448 key exchange as defined in RFC 7748. Inputs and outputs use the standard 56-byte little-endian encodings for X448. Return type is void; no status is reported.
requirements: q must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least CURVE448_SIZE (56) writable bytes.
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least CURVE448_SIZE (56) readable bytes containing the scalar in little-endian format (RFC 7748 encoding).
Buffers must not be under-allocated; passing shorter buffers results in out-of-bounds writes/reads.
The function does not report errors; callers should not assume success can be determined from the return value (there is none).

If the scalar clamping/formatting requirements are not handled by the caller, behavior is library-defined; whether clamping is performed internally is unknown from this header—callers should provide a properly formed X448 private scalar if required by their usage.
When used for key agreement, callers should follow RFC 7748 guidance (e.g., ensure the derived public key is used per protocol requirements).

functions.name: curve448_mul
functions.signature: void curve448_mul(uint8_t *q, const uint8_t *n, const uint8_t *p);
functions.description: Computes a Curve448/X448 scalar multiplication of an arbitrary point p by the scalar n, writing the 56-byte u-coordinate result to q. Typical usage: compute an X448 shared secret by multiplying a peer’s 56-byte public key (u-coordinate) by the caller’s 56-byte private scalar. Inputs and outputs use the standard 56-byte little-endian encodings for X448. Return type is void; no status is reported.
requirements: q must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least CURVE448_SIZE (56) writable bytes.
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least CURVE448_SIZE (56) readable bytes containing the scalar in little-endian format (RFC 7748 encoding).
p must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least CURVE448_SIZE (56) readable bytes containing the u-coordinate of a Curve448 point in little-endian format (RFC 7748 encoding).
Buffers must not be under-allocated; passing shorter buffers results in out-of-bounds writes/reads.
The function does not report errors; callers should not assume success can be determined from the return value (there is none).
Input validation of p (e.g., whether it encodes a valid point) is not specified by this header; callers should be prepared for library-defined handling of invalid points.
For X448 key agreement per RFC 7748, callers should verify that the output is not the all-zero value before using it as a shared secret; if all-zero, treat as a failure and discard the key exchange.
Whether scalar clamping/formatting is performed internally is not specified; callers should provide a properly formed X448 private scalar if required by their usage.

functions.name: des_set_key
functions.signature: int des_set_key(struct des_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a DES context with the 8-byte key and expands it into round keys. Returns 1 for acceptable (non-weak) keys and 0 for weak keys. Typical usage: call before any des_encrypt/des_decrypt operations using the same ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct des_ctx.
key must point to at least DES_KEY_SIZE (8) bytes.
Caller should check the return value and reject or handle weak keys when 0 is returned before using the context.
ctx must be successfully initialized by this function before being used with des_encrypt or des_decrypt.

functions.name: des_encrypt
functions.signature: void des_encrypt(const struct des_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts data in ECB-like blocks using DES. Processes length bytes from src into dst using the expanded key in ctx. Intended for whole-block processing; higher-level modes (CBC/CTR, etc.) should be built around this primitive.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct des_ctx previously initialized with des_set_key and not reported as weak if the application disallows weak keys.
length should be a multiple of DES_BLOCK_SIZE (8) bytes (inferred from block-cipher API and DES block size).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers of at least length bytes.

functions.name: des_decrypt
functions.signature: void des_decrypt(const struct des_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts data in ECB-like blocks using DES. Processes length bytes from src into dst using the expanded key in ctx. Intended for whole-block processing; use within a mode of operation as needed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct des_ctx previously initialized with des_set_key and not reported as weak if the application disallows weak keys.
length should be a multiple of DES_BLOCK_SIZE (8) bytes (inferred from block-cipher API and DES block size).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers of at least length bytes.

functions.name: des_check_parity
functions.signature: int des_check_parity(size_t length, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Checks DES key byte parity over length bytes, typically verifying odd parity for each byte as required by the DES standard. Returns nonzero if parity is correct, zero otherwise. Useful before or after key loading to validate key material.
requirements: key must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
length specifies the number of key bytes to check; for a single DES key this is typically DES_KEY_SIZE (8), for 3DES 24.
Caller should examine the return value to determine whether parity is acceptable.

functions.name: des_fix_parity
functions.signature: void des_fix_parity(size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Adjusts the parity of each of the length key bytes in src (typically to DES-required odd parity) and writes the result to dst.
requirements: src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
length specifies the number of bytes to adjust; for a single DES key this is typically DES_KEY_SIZE (8), for 3DES 24.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.

functions.name: des3_set_key
functions.signature: int des3_set_key(struct des3_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Triple-DES (EDE) context from a 24-byte key, setting up three internal DES subkeys. Returns 1 for acceptable (non-weak) keys and 0 for weak keys. Typical usage: call before any des3_encrypt/des3_decrypt operations using the same ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct des3_ctx.
key must point to at least DES3_KEY_SIZE (24) bytes.
Caller should check the return value and reject or handle weak keys when 0 is returned before using the context.
ctx must be successfully initialized by this function before being used with des3_encrypt or des3_decrypt.

functions.name: des3_encrypt
functions.signature: void des3_encrypt(const struct des3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts data in ECB-like blocks using Triple-DES (DES-EDE). Processes length bytes from src into dst using the expanded keys in ctx. Intended for whole-block processing; combine with a block mode as needed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct des3_ctx previously initialized with des3_set_key and not reported as weak if the application disallows weak keys.
length should be a multiple of DES3_BLOCK_SIZE (8) bytes (inferred from block-cipher API and DES block size).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers of at least length bytes.

functions.name: des3_decrypt
functions.signature: void des3_decrypt(const struct des3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts data in ECB-like blocks using Triple-DES (DES-EDE). Processes length bytes from src into dst using the expanded keys in ctx. Intended for whole-block processing; combine with a block mode as needed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct des3_ctx previously initialized with des3_set_key and not reported as weak if the application disallows weak keys.
length should be a multiple of DES3_BLOCK_SIZE (8) bytes (inferred from block-cipher API and DES block size).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers of at least length bytes.

functions.name: dsa_params_init
functions.signature: void dsa_params_init (struct dsa_params *params);
functions.description: Initializes a dsa_params structure by setting up internal bignums (p, q, g). Use before any other use of params. Counterpart is dsa_params_clear.
requirements: params must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory.
Call exactly once before using params with other DSA routines.
Call dsa_params_clear on the same object to release resources.

functions.name: dsa_params_clear
functions.signature: void dsa_params_clear (struct dsa_params *params);
functions.description: Releases bignum storage held by a dsa_params previously initialized with dsa_params_init.
requirements: params must be a non-NULL pointer previously initialized with dsa_params_init.
Do not use params after clearing unless re-initialized.
Safe to call exactly once per corresponding init; behavior on multiple clears is undefined.

functions.name: dsa_signature_init
functions.signature: void dsa_signature_init(struct dsa_signature *signature);
functions.description: Initializes a dsa_signature by calling mpz_init on r and s. Must be paired with dsa_signature_clear.
requirements: signature must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory.
Call before passing signature to operations that fill r and s (e.g., dsa_sign, decoders).
Call dsa_signature_clear to release allocated bignum storage.

functions.name: dsa_signature_clear
functions.signature: void dsa_signature_clear(struct dsa_signature *signature);
functions.description: Clears and frees bignum storage (r, s) in a dsa_signature previously initialized with dsa_signature_init.
requirements: signature must be non-NULL and previously initialized with dsa_signature_init.
Do not access r or s after clearing unless reinitialized.

functions.name: dsa_sign
functions.signature: int dsa_sign(const struct dsa_params *params, const mpz_t x, void *random_ctx, nettle_random_func *random, size_t digest_size, const uint8_t *digest, struct dsa_signature *signature);
functions.description: Computes a DSA signature over the provided message digest using private key x and domain parameters params. The signature (r,s) is written to signature.
requirements: params must point to a valid, initialized DSA parameter set (p, q, g).
x must be an initialized mpz_t holding the private key corresponding to params (typically 0 < x < q).
random and random_ctx must provide cryptographically strong random bytes; they are used to generate the per-message secret k (must be unpredictable and uniformly distributed modulo q).
digest must point to at least digest_size bytes; digest_size is the length of the message digest to be signed (implementation truncates per DSA rules; exact treatment not specified here).
signature must be initialized with dsa_signature_init before the call.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on error (caller should check the return value).

functions.name: dsa_verify
functions.signature: int dsa_verify(const struct dsa_params *params, const mpz_t y, size_t digest_size, const uint8_t *digest, const struct dsa_signature *signature);
functions.description: Verifies a DSA signature (r,s) over the provided message digest using public key y and domain parameters params.
requirements: params must point to a valid, initialized DSA parameter set (p, q, g).
y must be an initialized mpz_t holding the public key corresponding to params (typically y ≡ g^x mod p).
digest must point to at least digest_size bytes; digest_size is the length of the message digest used for verification (implementation may truncate per DSA rules; details not specified here).
signature must point to an initialized dsa_signature with valid r and s values.
Returns nonzero on successful verification, 0 on failure.

functions.name: dsa_generate_params
functions.signature: int dsa_generate_params(struct dsa_params *params, void *random_ctx, nettle_random_func *random, void *progress_ctx, nettle_progress_func *progress, unsigned p_bits, unsigned q_bits);
functions.description: Generates DSA domain parameters (p, q, g) of the requested sizes using the supplied randomness. Optionally reports progress via the progress callback.
requirements: params must be initialized with dsa_params_init and writable.
random and random_ctx must provide sufficient cryptographic randomness for parameter generation.
If provided, progress and progress_ctx must be valid for callback use; progress may be NULL if no progress reporting is desired.
p_bits and q_bits must be positive; typical FIPS-approved sizes exist (e.g., see DSA_SHA1_MIN_P_BITS, DSA_SHA256_Q_BITS), but exact constraints beyond bit-size are not specified here.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: dsa_generate_keypair
functions.signature: void dsa_generate_keypair (const struct dsa_params *params, mpz_t pub, mpz_t key, void *random_ctx, nettle_random_func *random);
functions.description: Generates a DSA keypair for the given domain parameters. Outputs private key in key and public key in pub.
requirements: params must be a valid, initialized DSA parameter set (p, q, g).
pub and key must be initialized mpz_t variables ready to receive results.
random and random_ctx must supply cryptographically strong randomness (used to sample the private key x in [1, q−1]).

functions.name: dsa_keypair_to_sexp
functions.signature: int dsa_keypair_to_sexp(struct nettle_buffer *buffer, const char *algorithm_name, const struct dsa_params *params, const mpz_t pub, const mpz_t priv);
functions.description: Serializes a DSA keypair (or public key only) to an S-expression and appends it to buffer. If priv is NULL, generates only a public-key expression. If algorithm_name is NULL, uses "dsa".
requirements: buffer must be a valid, initialized nettle_buffer with space policy as required by the nettle buffer API.
params must be initialized and consistent with the provided keys.
pub must be an initialized mpz_t public key value; required in all cases.
priv may be NULL (public-only output) or an initialized mpz_t containing the private key when producing a private-key expression.
algorithm_name may be NULL or a valid C string.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure (e.g., allocation/format errors).

functions.name: dsa_signature_from_sexp
functions.signature: int dsa_signature_from_sexp(struct dsa_signature *rs, struct sexp_iterator *i, unsigned q_bits);
functions.description: Parses a DSA signature from a S-expression provided by iterator i, storing components into rs, using q_bits as a size constraint for validation/truncation as appropriate.
requirements: rs must be initialized with dsa_signature_init before the call.
i must be a valid, positioned sexp_iterator referencing a DSA signature S-expression.
q_bits must be the expected bit length of the subgroup order q; must be positive.
Returns nonzero on successful parse, 0 on parse/validation failure.

functions.name: dsa_keypair_from_sexp_alist
functions.signature: int dsa_keypair_from_sexp_alist(struct dsa_params *params, mpz_t pub, mpz_t priv, unsigned p_max_bits, unsigned q_bits, struct sexp_iterator *i);
functions.description: Parses DSA key material from an S-expression alist using iterator i. Fills params and the provided pub/priv mpz_t values. Limits are enforced using p_max_bits and q_bits.
requirements: params must be initialized with dsa_params_init prior to the call.
pub and priv must be initialized mpz_t objects; either may be populated depending on the expression contents.
i must be a valid, positioned sexp_iterator over the key S-expression.
p_max_bits must be a positive limit on the size of p; q_bits must be the expected size of q in bits.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure (e.g., parse errors or exceeding limits).

functions.name: dsa_sha1_keypair_from_sexp
functions.signature: int dsa_sha1_keypair_from_sexp(struct dsa_params *params, mpz_t pub, mpz_t priv, unsigned p_max_bits, size_t length, const uint8_t *expr);
functions.description: Parses a DSA key from an S-expression blob using SHA-1 conventions. If priv is NULL, expects a public-key expression. If pub is NULL, expects a private-key expression and ignores parts not needed for the public key. Keys must be initialized before calling.
requirements: params must be initialized with dsa_params_init.
pub and/or priv must be initialized mpz_t as applicable; at least one must be non-NULL.
p_max_bits must be a positive cap on modulus size p.
expr must point to length bytes containing the S-expression.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on parse/validation failure.

functions.name: dsa_sha256_keypair_from_sexp
functions.signature: int dsa_sha256_keypair_from_sexp(struct dsa_params *params, mpz_t pub, mpz_t priv, unsigned p_max_bits, size_t length, const uint8_t *expr);
functions.description: Parses a DSA key from an S-expression blob using SHA-256 conventions. If priv is NULL, expects a public-key expression. If pub is NULL, expects a private-key expression and ignores parts not needed for the public key. Keys must be initialized before calling.
requirements: params must be initialized with dsa_params_init.
pub and/or priv must be initialized mpz_t as applicable; at least one must be non-NULL.
p_max_bits must be a positive cap on modulus size p.
expr must point to length bytes containing the S-expression.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on parse/validation failure.

functions.name: dsa_params_from_der_iterator
functions.signature: int dsa_params_from_der_iterator(struct dsa_params *params, unsigned max_bits, unsigned q_bits, struct asn1_der_iterator *i);
functions.description: Parses DSA domain parameters (p, q, g) from an ASN.1 DER stream using iterator i, enforcing size limits max_bits and q_bits.
requirements: params must be initialized with dsa_params_init.
i must be a valid, positioned asn1_der_iterator over the DSA parameters sequence.
max_bits must be a positive upper bound for p; q_bits must be the expected size of q in bits.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on parse/validation failure.

functions.name: dsa_public_key_from_der_iterator
functions.signature: int dsa_public_key_from_der_iterator(const struct dsa_params *params, mpz_t pub, struct asn1_der_iterator *i);
functions.description: Parses a DSA public key value from an ASN.1 DER stream using iterator i and writes it to pub, using params for context/validation.
requirements: params must point to a valid, initialized DSA parameter set.
pub must be an initialized mpz_t ready to receive the public key.
i must be a valid, positioned asn1_der_iterator over the public key encoding.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: dsa_openssl_private_key_from_der_iterator
functions.signature: int dsa_openssl_private_key_from_der_iterator(struct dsa_params *params, mpz_t pub, mpz_t priv, unsigned p_max_bits, struct asn1_der_iterator *i);
functions.description: Parses an OpenSSL-format DSA private key from an ASN.1 DER stream using iterator i. Fills params, priv, and pub (derived or parsed), enforcing modulus size limit p_max_bits.
requirements: params must be initialized with dsa_params_init before the call.
pub and priv must be initialized mpz_t objects ready to receive values.
p_max_bits must be a positive cap on the size of p.
i must be a valid, positioned asn1_der_iterator over the OpenSSL DSA private key structure.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on parse/validation failure.

functions.name: dsa_openssl_private_key_from_der
functions.signature: int dsa_openssl_private_key_from_der(struct dsa_params *params, mpz_t pub, mpz_t priv, unsigned p_max_bits, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Parses an OpenSSL-format DSA private key from a DER-encoded byte array. Populates params, priv, and pub, enforcing modulus size limit p_max_bits.
requirements: params must be initialized with dsa_params_init.
pub and priv must be initialized mpz_t objects.
data must point to length bytes containing the DER-encoded key.
p_max_bits must be a positive cap on the size of p.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure (e.g., malformed input or exceeding limits).

functions.name: eax_set_key
functions.signature: void eax_set_key(struct eax_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f);
functions.description: Initializes precomputed EAX pad values for a given 128-bit block cipher and key. The caller must provide a block-cipher context (cipher) already set up with the desired key and its encrypt function (f). Typically used once after setting the cipher key, before processing any nonce, associated data, or message.
requirements: cipher must be a valid, initialized block-cipher context keyed for encryption before calling this function.
f must point to the cipher’s encryption function with signature compatible with nettle_cipher_func (void (*)(void *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src)).
The underlying block cipher must have a 128-bit block size (as required by this EAX implementation).
key must be a valid, writable pointer to struct eax_key.

functions.name: eax_set_nonce
functions.signature: void eax_set_nonce(struct eax_ctx *eax, const struct eax_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t nonce_length, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Starts a new EAX session for a specific nonce (IV). Initializes the per-message EAX state using the precomputed key material and the provided nonce. Call this once per message before supplying AAD (update) or plaintext/ciphertext (encrypt/decrypt), then finish with eax_digest to get the authentication tag.
requirements: eax must be a valid, writable EAX state object.
key must have been initialized with eax_set_key using the same cipher and key.
cipher must be a valid, initialized 128-bit block-cipher context matching the key used with eax_set_key.
f must be the encrypt function for the provided cipher context.
nonce points to nonce_length bytes of nonce data; nonce_length may be zero or more (exact acceptable range is not documented here).
Do not reuse the same (key, nonce) pair across different messages (cryptographic requirement of EAX).

functions.name: eax_update
functions.signature: void eax_update(struct eax_ctx *eax, const struct eax_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t data_length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds associated data (AAD) into the EAX authentication state for the current message. This data is authenticated but not encrypted. Call after eax_set_nonce and before finalizing with eax_digest. It is typically called before encrypt/decrypt of the message payload.
requirements: eax must be initialized for the current message via eax_set_nonce.
key must be initialized via eax_set_key and correspond to the provided cipher and f.
cipher must be a valid, initialized 128-bit block-cipher context; f must be its encrypt function.
If data_length > 0, data must point to at least data_length bytes; if data_length == 0, data may be NULL.
May be called zero or more times prior to eax_digest; exact rules for interleaving with encrypt/decrypt are not specified here (use before digest at minimum).

functions.name: eax_encrypt
functions.signature: void eax_encrypt(struct eax_ctx *eax, const struct eax_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts plaintext to ciphertext for the current EAX message while updating the authentication state. Call after eax_set_nonce (and any eax_update for AAD) and before eax_digest. Produces dst = EAX-CTR(src) and authenticates the ciphertext/nonce/AAD.
requirements: eax must be initialized for the current message via eax_set_nonce.
key must be initialized via eax_set_key and correspond to the provided cipher and f.
cipher must be a valid, initialized 128-bit block-cipher context; f must be its encrypt function.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of plaintext and dst must point to at least length writable bytes.
Overlap behavior between dst and src is not specified in this header; to be safe, use non-overlapping buffers unless the implementation documents in-place operation.
May be called zero or more times to process the message; complete with eax_digest to obtain the tag.

functions.name: eax_decrypt
functions.signature: void eax_decrypt(struct eax_ctx *eax, const struct eax_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts ciphertext to plaintext for the current EAX message while updating the authentication state. Call after eax_set_nonce (and any eax_update for AAD) and before eax_digest. After all data is processed, call eax_digest and verify the tag before accepting the plaintext.
requirements: eax must be initialized for the current message via eax_set_nonce.
key must be initialized via eax_set_key and correspond to the provided cipher and f.
cipher must be a valid, initialized 128-bit block-cipher context; f must be its encrypt function.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of ciphertext and dst must point to at least length writable bytes.
Overlap behavior between dst and src is not specified in this header; to be safe, use non-overlapping buffers unless documented otherwise.
Decryption must be followed by computing and checking the EAX tag via eax_digest to ensure authenticity before using the plaintext.

functions.name: eax_digest
functions.signature: void eax_digest(struct eax_ctx *eax, const struct eax_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the current EAX computation and writes the authentication tag (MAC) to digest. Must be called after processing AAD (eax_update) and message data (eax_encrypt/eax_decrypt). The tag length is EAX_DIGEST_SIZE (16 bytes).
requirements: eax must be initialized for the current message via eax_set_nonce and updated with all AAD and message data intended for authentication.
key must be initialized via eax_set_key and correspond to the provided cipher and f.
cipher must be a valid, initialized 128-bit block-cipher context; f must be its encrypt function.
digest must point to at least EAX_DIGEST_SIZE (16) writable bytes.
Typically called once per message; behavior of multiple calls without reinitialization is not specified.

functions.name: eax_aes128_set_key
functions.signature: void eax_aes128_set_key(struct eax_aes128_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Convenience setup for EAX using AES-128. Initializes the combined EAX+AESCipher context with the provided 16-byte AES key and precomputes EAX key-dependent values.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to struct eax_aes128_ctx.
key must point to 16 bytes (128 bits) of key material.

functions.name: eax_aes128_set_nonce
functions.signature: void eax_aes128_set_nonce(struct eax_aes128_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *iv);
functions.description: Starts a new EAX-AES128 message with the given nonce (IV). After this call, you may supply AAD via eax_aes128_update and process data via eax_aes128_encrypt/decrypt, then finish with eax_aes128_digest.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via eax_aes128_set_key.
If length > 0, iv must point to at least length bytes; if length == 0, iv may be NULL.
Do not reuse the same (key, nonce) pair across different messages (cryptographic requirement of EAX).

functions.name: eax_aes128_update
functions.signature: void eax_aes128_update(struct eax_aes128_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds associated data (AAD) into the EAX-AES128 authentication state for the current message. Data is authenticated but not encrypted. Call before finalizing with eax_aes128_digest.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via eax_aes128_set_key and prepared for the current message via eax_aes128_set_nonce.
If length > 0, data must point to at least length bytes; if length == 0, data may be NULL.
May be called zero or more times prior to digest; exact interleaving rules with encrypt/decrypt are unspecified here (use before digest at minimum).

functions.name: eax_aes128_encrypt
functions.signature: void eax_aes128_encrypt(struct eax_aes128_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts plaintext to ciphertext under EAX-AES128 while updating the authentication state. Use after setting the nonce (and optionally providing AAD) and before obtaining the tag via eax_aes128_digest.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via eax_aes128_set_key and prepared via eax_aes128_set_nonce for the current message.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes and dst must point to at least length writable bytes.
Overlap behavior between dst and src is not specified in this header; to be safe, use non-overlapping buffers unless documented otherwise.
May be called zero or more times to process the message; complete with eax_aes128_digest to obtain the tag.

functions.name: eax_aes128_decrypt
functions.signature: void eax_aes128_decrypt(struct eax_aes128_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts ciphertext to plaintext under EAX-AES128 while updating the authentication state. After processing all data, call eax_aes128_digest and verify the tag before accepting the plaintext.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via eax_aes128_set_key and prepared via eax_aes128_set_nonce for the current message.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes and dst must point to at least length writable bytes.
Overlap behavior between dst and src is not specified in this header; to be safe, use non-overlapping buffers unless documented otherwise.
Decryption must be followed by computing and checking the EAX tag via eax_aes128_digest to ensure authenticity before using the plaintext.

functions.name: eax_aes128_digest
functions.signature: void eax_aes128_digest(struct eax_aes128_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes EAX-AES128 for the current message and writes the 16-byte authentication tag to digest.
requirements: ctx must have been prepared via eax_aes128_set_nonce and updated with all intended AAD and message data via eax_aes128_update and eax_aes128_encrypt/decrypt.
digest must point to at least EAX_DIGEST_SIZE (16) writable bytes.
Typically called once per message; behavior of multiple calls without reinitialization is not specified.

functions.name: ecc_point_init
functions.signature: void ecc_point_init (struct ecc_point *p, const struct ecc_curve *ecc);
functions.description: Initializes an ECC point structure for use on the specified curve. Allocates internal storage using GMP-compatible allocation and associates the point with the given curve.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-null pointer to struct ecc_point storage provided by the caller.
ecc must be a valid pointer to an ECC curve compatible with subsequent operations on this point.
Call ecc_point_clear on p when it is no longer needed to release allocated resources before reusing or freeing p.
The point is prepared for use with other ECC operations defined for the same curve; mixing curves is invalid.

functions.name: ecc_point_clear
functions.signature: void ecc_point_clear (struct ecc_point *p);
functions.description: Releases resources held by an ecc_point previously initialized with ecc_point_init. After this call, the point must not be used unless re-initialized.
requirements: p must have been previously initialized with ecc_point_init.
Do not use p after clearing it unless it is reinitialized.
p must not be cleared more than once without reinitialization.

functions.name: ecc_point_set
functions.signature: int ecc_point_set (struct ecc_point *p, const mpz_t x, const mpz_t y);
functions.description: Sets the affine coordinates (x,y) of point p on its associated curve. Returns non-zero on success, and zero if the coordinates do not represent a point on the curve.
requirements: p must be initialized with ecc_point_init and associated with a curve.
x and y must be initialized GMP integers (mpz_t).
The provided (x,y) must correspond to a point on the associated curve; otherwise the function fails and returns 0.

Most ECC functions do not support the point at infinity as input; representing infinity as x = 0 and y = 0 in affine coordinates is noted but should be avoided unless the consumer explicitly supports it.

functions.name: ecc_point_get
functions.signature: void ecc_point_get (const struct ecc_point *p, mpz_t x, mpz_t y);
functions.description: Exports the affine coordinates of point p into GMP integers x and y.
requirements: p must be initialized and must represent a valid, supported point on its associated curve.
x and y must be initialized GMP integers (mpz_t) ready to receive the coordinates.
Most ECC functions do not support the point at infinity as input or output; behavior for infinity is unspecified and should be avoided.

functions.name: ecc_scalar_init
functions.signature: void ecc_scalar_init (struct ecc_scalar *s, const struct ecc_curve *ecc);
functions.description: Initializes an ECC scalar structure associated with the specified curve’s group order. Allocates internal storage using GMP-compatible allocation.
requirements: s must be a valid, non-null pointer to struct ecc_scalar storage provided by the caller.
ecc must be a valid pointer to the ECC curve defining the scalar field (group order).
Call ecc_scalar_clear on s when it is no longer needed to release allocated resources before reuse or free.
Subsequent operations using this scalar must use the same curve association.

functions.name: ecc_scalar_clear
functions.signature: void ecc_scalar_clear (struct ecc_scalar *s);
functions.description: Releases resources held by an ecc_scalar previously initialized with ecc_scalar_init. After this call, the scalar must not be used unless re-initialized.
requirements: s must have been previously initialized with ecc_scalar_init.
Do not use s after clearing it unless it is reinitialized.
s must not be cleared more than once without reinitialization.

functions.name: ecc_scalar_set
functions.signature: int ecc_scalar_set (struct ecc_scalar *s, const mpz_t z);
functions.description: Sets scalar s from the GMP integer z, validating that it is in the proper range for the curve’s group order. Returns non-zero on success, zero on failure.
requirements: s must be initialized with ecc_scalar_init and associated with a curve.
z must be an initialized GMP integer (mpz_t).
z must be in the proper range for the curve’s group order; otherwise the function fails and returns 0.
The ecc_scalar type represents a non-zero scalar (element of Z_q^*); callers should not supply zero.

functions.name: ecc_scalar_get
functions.signature: void ecc_scalar_get (const struct ecc_scalar *s, mpz_t z);
functions.description: Exports the value of scalar s into GMP integer z.
requirements: s must be initialized with ecc_scalar_init and must contain a valid scalar value.
z must be an initialized GMP integer (mpz_t) ready to receive the value.

functions.name: ecc_scalar_random
functions.signature: void ecc_scalar_random (struct ecc_scalar *s, void *random_ctx, nettle_random_func *random);
functions.description: Generates a random non-zero scalar suitable for use as an ECDSA private key or ECDH exponent, using the provided random callback and context.
requirements: s must be initialized with ecc_scalar_init and associated with a curve.
random must be a valid function pointer of type nettle_random_func; it will be called with random_ctx to obtain randomness.
random must provide cryptographically secure random bytes sufficient for scalar generation.
The resulting scalar will be in the valid range for the curve’s group order and non-zero.

functions.name: ecc_point_mul
functions.signature: void ecc_point_mul (struct ecc_point *r, const struct ecc_scalar *n, const struct ecc_point *p);
functions.description: Computes the scalar multiplication r = n * p on the associated curve.
requirements: r must be initialized with ecc_point_init and associated with the same curve as n and p.
n must be an initialized ecc_scalar associated with the same curve and contain a valid (non-zero, in-range) value.
p must be an initialized ecc_point on the same curve and represent a supported (non-infinity) point.
Most ECC functions do not support the point at infinity as input or output; callers should avoid providing infinity and should not rely on receiving infinity as a result.

functions.name: ecc_point_mul_g
functions.signature: void ecc_point_mul_g (struct ecc_point *r, const struct ecc_scalar *n);
functions.description: Computes r = n * G, where G is the standard generator/base point of the curve associated with n (and r).
requirements: r must be initialized with ecc_point_init and associated with the same curve as n.
n must be an initialized ecc_scalar associated with the curve and contain a valid (non-zero, in-range) value.
Most ECC functions do not support the point at infinity as output; with non-zero n, r should be a valid, non-infinity point.

functions.name: ecc_bit_size
functions.signature: unsigned ecc_bit_size (const struct ecc_curve *ecc);
functions.description: Returns the bit size of a single coordinate on the given curve (and the prime p).
requirements: ecc must be a valid pointer to an ECC curve.

functions.name: ecc_size
functions.signature: mp_size_t ecc_size (const struct ecc_curve *ecc);
functions.description: Returns the limb count (size) of a single coordinate for the given curve, in units of mp_limb_t.
requirements: ecc must be a valid pointer to an ECC curve.

functions.name: ecc_size_a
functions.signature: mp_size_t ecc_size_a (const struct ecc_curve *ecc);
functions.description: Returns the limb count (size) for a point in affine coordinates (x,y) for the given curve.
requirements: ecc must be a valid pointer to an ECC curve.

functions.name: ecc_size_j
functions.signature: mp_size_t ecc_size_j (const struct ecc_curve *ecc);
functions.description: Returns the limb count (size) for a point in Jacobian coordinates (X,Y,Z) for the given curve.
requirements: ecc must be a valid pointer to an ECC curve.

functions.name: ecdsa_sign
functions.signature: void ecdsa_sign(const struct ecc_scalar *key, void *random_ctx, nettle_random_func *random, size_t digest_length, const uint8_t *digest, struct dsa_signature *signature)
functions.description: Computes an ECDSA signature over the provided message digest using the given private key (ecc_scalar). The signature is written to the provided dsa_signature object. A caller-supplied cryptographic RNG (context and callback) is used internally to generate the per-message nonce. Typical usage: initialize/associate key with a curve, hash your message to get a digest, then call to produce (r,s) in signature. Details such as digest truncation to the curve order are implementation-defined and not specified in this header.
requirements: key must reference a valid, initialized private ECDSA key (ecc_scalar) bound to a specific curve.
random must be a cryptographically secure RNG function compatible with nettle_random_func; random_ctx must be a valid context for that function.
digest must point to digest_length bytes of initialized data representing the hash of the message to be signed.
signature must point to an initialized dsa_signature structure where the function can store the result.
The key and the signature’s implied curve must match; both must use the same elliptic curve.
The function does not return an error code; callers must assume it succeeds if inputs satisfy the library’s preconditions. Any error reporting beyond that is unknown.

functions.name: ecdsa_verify
functions.signature: int ecdsa_verify(const struct ecc_point *pub, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest, const struct dsa_signature *signature)
functions.description: Verifies an ECDSA signature against the provided message digest using the given public key (ecc_point). Returns non-zero if the signature verifies, and 0 otherwise. Typical usage: provide a valid public key on the same curve as the signature, the message digest, and the (r,s) signature.
requirements: pub must reference a valid, initialized ECDSA public key (ecc_point) on the correct curve for the signature.
digest must point to length bytes of initialized data representing the message hash.
signature must point to a valid, initialized dsa_signature containing ECDSA components (r,s) for the same curve as pub.
Return value: non-zero indicates a valid signature; 0 indicates verification failure.

functions.name: ecdsa_generate_keypair
functions.signature: void ecdsa_generate_keypair(struct ecc_point *pub, struct ecc_scalar *key, void *random_ctx, nettle_random_func *random)
functions.description: Generates a new ECDSA keypair on the curve associated with the provided ecc_scalar/ecc_point objects. The private key (ecc_scalar) is generated randomly and the corresponding public key (ecc_point) is computed. RNG is provided by caller via random/random_ctx. Typical usage: allocate and initialize key and pub for a chosen curve, then call to fill them.
requirements: pub must be an initialized ecc_point associated with the same curve as key and suitable for receiving the public key.
key must be an initialized ecc_scalar associated with the intended curve; on return, it contains a new private key value.
random must be a cryptographically secure RNG function compatible with nettle_random_func; random_ctx must be a valid context for that function.
pub and key must refer to the same curve; mixing curves is invalid.
The function does not return an error code; failure handling (if any) is unknown.

functions.name: ecc_ecdsa_sign_itch
functions.signature: mp_size_t ecc_ecdsa_sign_itch(const struct ecc_curve *ecc)
functions.description: Returns the size, in mp_limb_t units, of the scratch workspace required by ecc_ecdsa_sign for the given curve. Use this to allocate the scratch buffer before calling ecc_ecdsa_sign.
requirements: ecc must point to a valid, initialized ecc_curve describing the target curve.
The returned value is the minimum number of mp_limb_t elements required for the scratch buffer passed to ecc_ecdsa_sign.

functions.name: ecc_ecdsa_sign
functions.signature: void ecc_ecdsa_sign(const struct ecc_curve *ecc, const mp_limb_t *zp, const mp_limb_t *kp, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest, mp_limb_t *rp, mp_limb_t *sp, mp_limb_t *scratch)
functions.description: Low-level ECDSA signing primitive operating on GMP-style limb arrays. Computes (r,s) given a curve, a private scalar zp, a per-message random nonce kp, and a message digest. Results are written to rp and sp. Caller must supply a scratch workspace sized by ecc_ecdsa_sign_itch(ecc).
requirements: ecc must point to a valid ecc_curve for which all other parameters are sized and interpreted.
zp must point to the private key scalar represented in mp_limb_t array form, sized appropriately for the curve order.
kp must point to a random per-message nonce scalar in mp_limb_t array form that is invertible modulo the curve group order (i.e., gcd(k, n) = 1); non-invertible nonces are invalid.
digest must point to length bytes of the message hash; how it is mapped/truncated to the group order is implementation-defined (unknown here).
rp and sp must point to output buffers (mp_limb_t arrays) large enough to hold scalars modulo the curve order for ecc.
scratch must point to a workspace buffer of at least ecc_ecdsa_sign_itch(ecc) mp_limb_t elements.
All inputs must correspond to the same curve and use consistent limb sizes and endianness conventions for the library (exact representation details are unspecified here).

functions.name: ecc_ecdsa_verify_itch
functions.signature: mp_size_t ecc_ecdsa_verify_itch(const struct ecc_curve *ecc)
functions.description: Returns the size, in mp_limb_t units, of the scratch workspace required by ecc_ecdsa_verify for the given curve. Use this value to allocate the scratch buffer before verification.
requirements: ecc must point to a valid, initialized ecc_curve describing the target curve.
The returned value is the minimum number of mp_limb_t elements required for the scratch buffer passed to ecc_ecdsa_verify.

functions.name: ecc_ecdsa_verify
functions.signature: int ecc_ecdsa_verify(const struct ecc_curve *ecc, const mp_limb_t *pp, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest, const mp_limb_t *rp, const mp_limb_t *sp, mp_limb_t *scratch)
functions.description: Low-level ECDSA verification primitive using limb arrays. Verifies signature components (r,s) over the provided digest using the given public key pp on curve ecc. Returns non-zero if the signature is valid, 0 otherwise. Requires a scratch workspace sized by ecc_ecdsa_verify_itch(ecc).
requirements: ecc must point to a valid ecc_curve.
pp must point to a valid public key represented as mp_limb_t array(s) consistent with ecc (exact layout unspecified here).
digest must point to length bytes of the message hash.
rp and sp must point to the signature scalar components as mp_limb_t arrays sized for the curve order.
scratch must point to a workspace buffer of at least ecc_ecdsa_verify_itch(ecc) mp_limb_t elements.
Return value: non-zero indicates the signature verifies; 0 indicates failure.
All inputs must correspond to the same curve and use consistent limb sizes and representation; exact encoding details are unspecified here.

functions.name: ed25519_sha512_public_key
functions.signature: void ed25519_sha512_public_key(uint8_t *pub, const uint8_t *priv);
functions.description: Computes the Ed25519 public key from a 32-byte private key seed using SHA-512. Intended usage: allocate a 32-byte buffer for pub, pass a 32-byte private key seed in priv, and call once to derive the corresponding public key. Output is written to pub. Details of key encoding follow Nettle’s Ed25519 implementation; exact encoding specifics are not documented here.
requirements: pub must point to a writable buffer of at least ED25519_KEY_SIZE (32) bytes.
priv must point to a readable buffer of exactly ED25519_KEY_SIZE (32) bytes representing the Ed25519 private key/seed.
Pointers must be non-NULL.
Function does not return a status; callers should assume it always writes ED25519_KEY_SIZE bytes to pub.

functions.name: ed25519_sha512_sign
functions.signature: void ed25519_sha512_sign(const uint8_t *pub, const uint8_t *priv, size_t length, const uint8_t *msg, uint8_t *signature);
functions.description: Generates an Ed25519 signature (64 bytes) over the message msg[0..length-1] using the provided private key seed and corresponding public key, with SHA-512 per Ed25519. Expected usage: derive pub from priv using ed25519_sha512_public_key, then call this function to produce signature into a 64-byte buffer.
requirements: pub must point to a readable buffer of ED25519_KEY_SIZE (32) bytes holding the public key corresponding to priv (inferred from API design).
priv must point to a readable buffer of ED25519_KEY_SIZE (32) bytes representing the Ed25519 private key/seed.
signature must point to a writable buffer of at least ED25519_SIGNATURE_SIZE (64) bytes.
msg must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes; length may be zero. For portability, pass a non-NULL msg even when length is 0 (NULL allowance is unspecified).
All pointer arguments must be non-NULL.
The public key must match the private key; mismatched keys result in an invalid signature (inferred).

functions.name: ed25519_sha512_verify
functions.signature: int ed25519_sha512_verify(const uint8_t *pub, size_t length, const uint8_t *msg, const uint8_t *signature);
functions.description: Verifies an Ed25519-SHA512 signature over msg[0..length-1] using the given public key. Returns a status indicating whether signature is valid for the message and key. Intended usage: provide the 32-byte public key, the message and its length, and a 64-byte signature to check.
requirements: pub must point to a readable buffer of ED25519_KEY_SIZE (32) bytes.
signature must point to a readable buffer of ED25519_SIGNATURE_SIZE (64) bytes.
msg must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes; length may be zero. For portability, pass a non-NULL msg even when length is 0 (NULL allowance is unspecified).
All pointer arguments must be non-NULL.
Return value convention is not explicitly documented; by Nettle convention, non-zero indicates a valid signature and zero indicates failure (inferred).

functions.name: ed448_shake256_public_key
functions.signature: void ed448_shake256_public_key(uint8_t *pub, const uint8_t *priv);
functions.description: Computes the Ed448 public key from a 57-byte private key seed using SHAKE256. Intended usage: allocate a 57-byte buffer for pub, pass a 57-byte private key seed in priv, and call to derive the corresponding public key. Output is written to pub. Encoding specifics follow Nettle’s Ed448 implementation; exact details are not documented here.
requirements: pub must point to a writable buffer of at least ED448_KEY_SIZE (57) bytes.
priv must point to a readable buffer of exactly ED448_KEY_SIZE (57) bytes representing the Ed448 private key/seed.
Pointers must be non-NULL.
Function does not return a status; callers should assume it always writes ED448_KEY_SIZE bytes to pub.

functions.name: ed448_shake256_sign
functions.signature: void ed448_shake256_sign(const uint8_t *pub, const uint8_t *priv, size_t length, const uint8_t *msg, uint8_t *signature);
functions.description: Generates an Ed448 signature (114 bytes) over the message msg[0..length-1] using the provided private key seed and corresponding public key, with SHAKE256 per Ed448. Expected usage: derive pub from priv using ed448_shake256_public_key, then call this function to produce signature into a 114-byte buffer.
requirements: pub must point to a readable buffer of ED448_KEY_SIZE (57) bytes holding the public key corresponding to priv (inferred from API design).
priv must point to a readable buffer of ED448_KEY_SIZE (57) bytes representing the Ed448 private key/seed.
signature must point to a writable buffer of at least ED448_SIGNATURE_SIZE (114) bytes.
msg must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes; length may be zero. For portability, pass a non-NULL msg even when length is 0 (NULL allowance is unspecified).
All pointer arguments must be non-NULL.
The public key must match the private key; mismatched keys result in an invalid signature (inferred).

functions.name: ed448_shake256_verify
functions.signature: int ed448_shake256_verify(const uint8_t *pub, size_t length, const uint8_t *msg, const uint8_t *signature);
functions.description: Verifies an Ed448-SHAKE256 signature over msg[0..length-1] using the given public key. Returns a status indicating whether signature is valid for the message and key. Intended usage: provide the 57-byte public key, the message and its length, and a 114-byte signature to check.
requirements: pub must point to a readable buffer of ED448_KEY_SIZE (57) bytes.
signature must point to a readable buffer of ED448_SIGNATURE_SIZE (114) bytes.
msg must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes; length may be zero. For portability, pass a non-NULL msg even when length is 0 (NULL allowance is unspecified).
All pointer arguments must be non-NULL.
Return value convention is not explicitly documented; by Nettle convention, non-zero indicates a valid signature and zero indicates failure (inferred).

functions.name: gcm_set_key
functions.signature: void gcm_set_key(struct gcm_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f);
functions.description: Initializes the GCM hashing subkey (H) in key using the provided block cipher instance and its encrypt function. Call this once per secret key before processing any messages with that key.
requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer to struct gcm_key.
cipher must point to an initialized block cipher context configured with the desired secret key.
f must be the cipher’s block-encrypt function compatible with cipher.
The cipher’s block size must be 16 bytes (GCM_BLOCK_SIZE).
Must be called before gcm_set_iv/gcm_update/gcm_encrypt/gcm_decrypt/gcm_digest for a given key.

functions.name: gcm_set_iv
functions.signature: void gcm_set_iv(struct gcm_ctx *ctx, const struct gcm_key *key, size_t length, const uint8_t *iv);
functions.description: Initializes per-message GCM state in ctx for the supplied IV/nonce. Must be called for each message before processing associated data or plaintext/ciphertext.
requirements: ctx must point to a writable struct gcm_ctx for this message.
key must point to a gcm_key previously initialized via gcm_set_key with the same cipher key.
If length > 0, iv must point to at least length bytes of IV data.
Must be called before gcm_update/gcm_encrypt/gcm_decrypt/gcm_digest for the current message.

IV length is in bytes; exact allowed sizes are cipher- and GCM-specific (commonly any length, with 12 preferred); behavior for other lengths follows GCM, but exact handling details are not documented here.

functions.name: gcm_update
functions.signature: void gcm_update(struct gcm_ctx *ctx, const struct gcm_key *key, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds Additional Authenticated Data (AAD) into the ongoing GCM computation. Can be called zero or more times after gcm_set_iv and before or interleaved with encryption/decryption.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for the current message with gcm_set_iv.
key must be the same gcm_key used to initialize this message.
If length > 0, data must point to at least length bytes of AAD.
May be called multiple times; length may be any non-negative size.

functions.name: gcm_encrypt
functions.signature: void gcm_encrypt(struct gcm_ctx *ctx, const struct gcm_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts plaintext src to ciphertext dst under the current GCM state, updating authentication state. Can be called multiple times per message.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for the current message with gcm_set_iv.
key must be a gcm_key initialized with gcm_set_key using the same cipher key as cipher.
cipher must point to an initialized 16-byte block cipher context; f must be its encrypt function.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes; dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
dst and src must be valid for the given length; in-place operation (dst==src) is not documented here; if unsure, use separate buffers.
May be interleaved with gcm_update calls as permitted by GCM.

functions.name: gcm_decrypt
functions.signature: void gcm_decrypt(struct gcm_ctx *ctx, const struct gcm_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts ciphertext src to plaintext dst under the current GCM state, updating authentication state. Can be called multiple times per message.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for the current message with gcm_set_iv.
key must be a gcm_key initialized with gcm_set_key using the same cipher key as cipher.
cipher must point to an initialized 16-byte block cipher context; f must be its encrypt function (GCM uses encryption primitive for both directions).
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes; dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
dst and src must be valid for the given length; in-place operation (dst==src) is not documented here; if unsure, use separate buffers.

functions.name: gcm_digest
functions.signature: void gcm_digest(struct gcm_ctx *ctx, const struct gcm_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the current GCM message and writes the 16-byte authentication tag to digest.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with gcm_set_iv and used for any desired gcm_update/gcm_encrypt/gcm_decrypt calls for this message.
key must match the key used for this message; cipher and f must match the cipher context and encrypt function used for this message.
digest must point to at least GCM_DIGEST_SIZE (16) writable bytes.
Should be called after all AAD and data processing for the message. Subsequent use of ctx for a new message requires a new gcm_set_iv.

functions.name: gcm_aes128_set_key
functions.signature: void gcm_aes128_set_key(struct gcm_aes128_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes an all-in-one AES-128-GCM context with the provided 128-bit key.
requirements: ctx must point to a writable struct gcm_aes128_ctx.
key must point to at least 16 bytes (128 bits).
Must be called before gcm_aes128_set_iv/update/encrypt/decrypt/digest.

functions.name: gcm_aes128_update
functions.signature: void gcm_aes128_update(struct gcm_aes128_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds AAD into an AES-128-GCM context initialized for the current message.
requirements: ctx must have been set up with gcm_aes128_set_key and gcm_aes128_set_iv for this message.
If length > 0, data must point to at least length bytes.
May be called multiple times.

functions.name: gcm_aes128_set_iv
functions.signature: void gcm_aes128_set_iv(struct gcm_aes128_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *iv);
functions.description: Sets the IV/nonce for the next AES-128-GCM message and initializes per-message state.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with gcm_aes128_set_key.
If length > 0, iv must point to at least length bytes.
Must be called before update/encrypt/decrypt/digest for each message.

functions.name: gcm_aes128_encrypt
