functions.name: gosthash94_init
functions.signature: void gosthash94_init(struct gosthash94_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a GOST R 34.11-94 hash context. Call this before feeding data to compute a 256-bit (32-byte) digest. After initialization, use gosthash94_update (or the CryptoPro variant consistently) to supply data, then gosthash94_digest to obtain the hash.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct gosthash94_ctx.
Must be called before any corresponding gosthash94_update/gosthash94_digest on the same ctx.
The same ctx must not be accessed concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.
Do not mix the regular and CryptoPro (gosthash94cp_*) update/digest functions on the same ctx; initialize and use one variant consistently (inferred from API split).

functions.name: gosthash94_update
functions.signature: void gosthash94_update(struct gosthash94_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *msg);
functions.description: Absorbs message bytes into an initialized GOST R 34.11-94 hash context using the standard parameter set. Can be called multiple times to process data in chunks. Finalize with gosthash94_digest to get the 32-byte result.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized gosthash94_ctx (initialized by gosthash94_init).
If length > 0, msg must point to at least length bytes of readable memory; if length == 0, msg may be NULL.
length is the number of bytes to process and must fit in size_t.
Do not mix with gosthash94cp_update/gosthash94cp_digest on the same ctx (use one variant consistently; inferred from API split).
The same ctx must not be accessed concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: gosthash94_digest
functions.signature: void gosthash94_digest(struct gosthash94_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *result);
functions.description: Finalizes the GOST R 34.11-94 computation with the standard parameter set and writes the 32-byte digest to result. Intended to be called after one or more gosthash94_update calls.
requirements: ctx must be a valid gosthash94_ctx that has been initialized with gosthash94_init (and optionally updated with gosthash94_update).
result must point to a writable buffer of at least GOSTHASH94_DIGEST_SIZE (32) bytes.
Do not mix with gosthash94cp_update/gosthash94cp_digest on the same ctx (use one variant consistently; inferred).

Behavior of the ctx after this call (whether it can be reused for further updates) is unspecified by this header; callers should reinitialize with gosthash94_init if reuse is needed (inferred as unknown).
The same ctx must not be accessed concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: gosthash94cp_update
functions.signature: void gosthash94cp_update(struct gosthash94_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *msg);
functions.description: Absorbs message bytes into an initialized GOST R 34.11-94 hash context using the CryptoPro S-box parameter set ("cp" variant). Use this for the CryptoPro version of the hash. Finalize with gosthash94cp_digest.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized gosthash94_ctx (initialized via gosthash94_init or the alias gosthash94cp_init).
If length > 0, msg must point to at least length bytes of readable memory; if length == 0, msg may be NULL.
length is the number of bytes to process and must fit in size_t.
Do not mix cp and non-cp update/digest functions on the same ctx; use gosthash94cp_update only with gosthash94cp_digest (inferred from API split).
The same ctx must not be accessed concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: gosthash94cp_digest
functions.signature: void gosthash94cp_digest(struct gosthash94_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *result);
functions.description: Finalizes the GOST R 34.11-94 computation using the CryptoPro parameter set and writes the 32-byte digest to result. Intended to be called after one or more gosthash94cp_update calls.
requirements: ctx must be a valid gosthash94_ctx initialized via gosthash94_init/gosthash94cp_init and updated with gosthash94cp_update.
result must point to a writable buffer of at least GOSTHASH94CP_DIGEST_SIZE (32) bytes.
Do not mix cp and non-cp update/digest functions on the same ctx (use the cp variant consistently; inferred).
Behavior of the ctx after this call (whether it can be reused for further updates) is unspecified by this header; callers should reinitialize if reuse is needed (inferred as unknown).
The same ctx must not be accessed concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: hkdf_extract
functions.signature:
void hkdf_extract(void *mac_ctx,
             nettle_hash_update_func *update,
             nettle_hash_digest_func *digest,
             size_t secret_size, const uint8_t *secret,
             uint8_t *dst);
functions.description: Computes the HKDF-Extract step (RFC 5869) using the caller-provided MAC context and operations. The function HMACs the input secret (IKM) with the MAC context’s current key (typically the HKDF salt) and writes the pseudorandom key (PRK) to dst. Intended usage: initialize mac_ctx for the chosen HMAC/hash (keyed with the salt, which may be empty), then call hkdf_extract with the input keying material; copy the resulting PRK from dst for later use (e.g., to key hkdf_expand). Notes: The digest size is implied by the provided MAC implementation; the function does not return a status code and is expected to always produce exactly one MAC-sized PRK.
requirements: mac_ctx must point to a valid MAC/HMAC context compatible with update and digest, already initialized/keyed (typically with the HKDF salt; empty salt is allowed by HKDF).
update and digest must be non-null and must be the correct function pointers for the MAC implementation underlying mac_ctx.
secret must point to a readable buffer of length secret_size when secret_size > 0; it may be NULL if secret_size == 0.
dst must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the MAC output length for the chosen hash (i.e., HashLen bytes).
The MAC output length (HashLen) is determined by mac_ctx/update/digest; callers must know this size to allocate dst appropriately.
mac_ctx may be modified by this call; do not use the same mac_ctx concurrently from multiple threads or interleave with other MAC operations without reinitializing as required by the MAC API.
The function returns void and does not report errors; callers must ensure all preconditions are met.

functions.name: hkdf_expand
functions.signature:
void hkdf_expand(void *mac_ctx,
            nettle_hash_update_func *update,
            nettle_hash_digest_func *digest,
            size_t digest_size,
            size_t info_size, const uint8_t *info,
            size_t length, uint8_t *dst);
functions.description: Computes the HKDF-Expand step (RFC 5869) using the caller-provided MAC context and operations to generate length bytes of output keying material (OKM) into dst. The MAC context must be keyed with the pseudorandom key (PRK) produced by hkdf_extract. Optional context/application info may be provided via info/info_size. Intended usage: key mac_ctx with PRK, then call hkdf_expand with the desired digest_size (MAC output length for the chosen hash), optional info, and target length; the function fills dst with OKM. Notes: length may span multiple MAC blocks; HKDF limits length to 255*digest_size.
requirements: mac_ctx must point to a valid MAC/HMAC context compatible with update and digest, already initialized/keyed with the PRK from hkdf_extract.
update and digest must be non-null and must be the correct function pointers for the MAC implementation underlying mac_ctx.
digest_size must equal the MAC output length (HashLen) of the chosen hash/MAC; callers must supply the correct value.
info must point to a readable buffer of length info_size when info_size > 0; it may be NULL if info_size == 0 (HKDF permits empty info).
dst must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes; the function writes exactly length bytes.
length must be in the HKDF-specified range 0 <= length <= 255 * digest_size; callers must enforce this to avoid invalid HKDF usage.
Do not call concurrently on the same mac_ctx; the context may be modified during the computation.
The function returns void and does not report errors; callers must ensure all preconditions are met.

functions.name: knuth_lfib_init

requirements: ctx must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory for a struct knuth_lfib_ctx.

functions.name: knuth_lfib_get
functions.signature: uint32_t knuth_lfib_get(struct knuth_lfib_ctx *ctx);

requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and must have been initialized by knuth_lfib_init before calling.
The function advances the internal state; repeated calls will produce a deterministic sequence based on the seed.
Return values are constrained to 0 .. 2^30-1 as documented.
Not suitable for cryptographic use.

a must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory capable of holding at least n uint32_t elements.

Not suitable for cryptographic use.

dst must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory with capacity for at least n bytes.
If n is 0, no bytes are written.
Not suitable for cryptographic use.

functions.name: md2_init
functions.signature: void md2_init(struct md2_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes an MD2 hashing context. Call this before supplying any input data via md2_update and before producing the final 16-byte MD2 digest with md2_digest. Typical usage: allocate a struct md2_ctx, call md2_init(&ctx), then one or more md2_update calls, and finally md2_digest(&ctx, out).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable struct md2_ctx.
Must be called before any md2_update or md2_digest on the same ctx.
The same ctx must not be accessed concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: md2_update
functions.signature: void md2_update(struct md2_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds input bytes into an ongoing MD2 hash computation. May be called zero or more times after md2_init and before md2_digest. Processes exactly length bytes from data, updating ctx accordingly.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer previously initialized with md2_init.
If length > 0, data must be a non-NULL pointer to at least length readable bytes.
May be called multiple times to hash input in chunks; ordering is preserved.
Do not call concurrently on the same ctx from multiple threads.

functions.name: md2_digest
functions.signature: void md2_digest(struct md2_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the MD2 computation and writes the 16-byte message digest to digest. Should be called after md2_init and after all desired md2_update calls. Behavior regarding whether the context is left in a reusable state is not specified in this header.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer that has been initialized with md2_init and optionally updated via md2_update.
digest must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least MD2_DIGEST_SIZE (16) bytes.
Do not assume the ctx can be reused after this call; if reuse is desired, reinitialize with md2_init unless documentation guarantees otherwise (unspecified here).
Do not call concurrently on the same ctx from multiple threads.

functions.name: md4_init
functions.signature: void md4_init(struct md4_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes an MD4 hashing context. Call this before feeding data with md4_update and finalizing with md4_digest. Sets the internal state, counters, and buffer to the MD4 initial values. Note: MD4 is cryptographically broken and should not be used for security-critical purposes; this API is typically for compatibility or testing.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable memory of type struct md4_ctx.
Must be called before any md4_update or md4_digest on the same context.
The function returns void and provides no error reporting.

functions.name: md4_update
functions.signature: void md4_update(struct md4_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds arbitrary-length input into an initialized MD4 context. May be called zero or more times to process streaming data. Internally updates the MD4 state and buffered block processing.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct md4_ctx previously initialized with md4_init.
If length > 0, data must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least length bytes of readable memory. If length == 0, data may be NULL (inferred typical convention).
May be called multiple times; the order of calls defines the byte sequence hashed.
The function returns void and provides no error reporting.
Do not modify ctx concurrently from multiple threads (per-context operations are not thread-safe unless externally synchronized; inference based on typical stateful hash contexts).

functions.name: md4_digest
functions.signature: void md4_digest(struct md4_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the hash and writes the 16-byte MD4 message digest to the provided buffer. Expected usage: md4_init → md4_update (0+ times) → md4_digest. It writes exactly MD4_DIGEST_SIZE (16) bytes. Post-call state handling (whether ctx is reset or only finalized) is not specified in this header and is therefore unknown.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct md4_ctx that has been initialized with md4_init. It should have received all input via md4_update before calling this function.
digest must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least MD4_DIGEST_SIZE (16) bytes of writable memory.
The function returns void and provides no error reporting.

The effect on ctx after this call (whether it is reusable for further updates or requires reinitialization) is unspecified by this header and should be treated as unknown; callers should conservatively reinitialize with md4_init before reusing.

functions.name: md5_init
functions.signature: void md5_init(struct md5_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes an MD5 context for hashing. Call this before any calls to md5_update or md5_digest to set up the internal state for a new MD5 computation. Typical usage: declare a struct md5_ctx, call md5_init, then feed data with md5_update and finish with md5_digest.
requirements: ctx must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory of type struct md5_ctx.
Must be called before the first md5_update or md5_digest that uses this ctx.
Do not use the same ctx concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: md5_update
functions.signature: void md5_update(struct md5_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds message data into an ongoing MD5 computation. Can be called zero or more times after md5_init to process streaming input in chunks of arbitrary size. The internal buffering handles non-block-sized input.
requirements: ctx must be a non-NULL pointer to a struct md5_ctx previously initialized with md5_init.
If length > 0, data must be a non-NULL pointer to at least length bytes of readable memory.
May be called multiple times to process a message in pieces; order of calls determines the byte sequence hashed.
Not safe for concurrent use on the same ctx without external synchronization.

functions.name: md5_digest
functions.signature: void md5_digest(struct md5_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the MD5 computation for the provided context and writes the 16-byte (MD5_DIGEST_SIZE) digest to the caller-provided buffer. Intended to be called after all md5_update calls for a message. Behavior regarding whether the context is reset for reuse is not specified in this header.
requirements: ctx must be a non-NULL pointer to a struct md5_ctx that has been initialized with md5_init (and optionally updated with md5_update).
digest must be a non-NULL pointer to at least MD5_DIGEST_SIZE (16) bytes of writable memory.
Call after all desired input has been provided via md5_update for the current message.
Do not use the same ctx concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.
Whether ctx remains valid for subsequent updates or is reinitialized is unknown from this header; callers should not assume either behavior without consulting the implementation.

functions.name: md5_compress

requirements: state must point to an array of 4 uint32_t words representing the current MD5 state.
data must point to exactly 64 bytes (MD5_BLOCK_SIZE) of readable input; the pointer may be unaligned.
Caller is responsible for providing correctly formatted MD5 state and block data; this function performs no length checks.
Not intended to be mixed arbitrarily with md5_update without understanding MD5’s internal block processing.

functions.name: memxor
functions.signature: void *memxor(void *dst, const void *src, size_t n);
functions.description: XORs n bytes from the source buffer into the destination buffer, byte-wise: for i in [0, n), dst[i] ^= src[i]. Returns dst. Intended for efficiently mixing or masking buffers (e.g., cryptographic constructions). Name is macro-mapped to nettle_memxor in this header.
requirements: dst must point to a writable memory region of at least n bytes.
src must point to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
If n is 0, the function performs no reads or writes and returns dst.
The function does not report errors; callers must ensure pointer validity and size correctness.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst regions is not documented here and should be treated as unknown/unspecified.

functions.name: memxor3

functions.description: Computes the byte-wise XOR of two input buffers into the destination: for i in [0, n), dst[i] = a[i] ^ b[i]. Returns dst. Useful for combining two buffers without modifying the inputs. Name is macro-mapped to nettle_memxor3 in this header.
requirements: dst must point to a writable memory region of at least n bytes.
a must point to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
b must point to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
If n is 0, the function performs no reads or writes and returns dst.
The function does not report errors; callers must ensure pointer validity and size correctness.
Behavior for overlapping regions between dst and a or b is not documented here and should be treated as unknown/unspecified.

functions.name: nist_keywrap16
functions.signature: void nist_keywrap16 (const void *ctx, nettle_cipher_func *encrypt, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ciphertext_length, uint8_t *ciphertext, const uint8_t *cleartext);
functions.description: Wraps key material using the NIST AES Key Wrap algorithm (RFC 3394), parameterized by a 16-byte block cipher provided via encrypt. Produces ciphertext_length bytes of wrapped data, which should be cleartext_length + 8. Use when you need to securely wrap a sequence of 8-byte blocks with an integrity check. The iv is the 8-byte initial value (default per RFC3394 is 0xA6 repeated; whether a NULL iv implies a default is unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid cipher context matching encrypt.
encrypt must point to a 16-byte block cipher encryption function compatible with ctx (AES-like, ECB single-block semantics).
iv must reference 8 bytes of initial value per RFC 3394.
ciphertext_length must be at least 16 and a multiple of 8.
cleartext must contain ciphertext_length - 8 bytes of input (a positive multiple of 8).
ciphertext must have space for ciphertext_length bytes of output.
Input cleartext length must be >= 8 bytes (at least one 64-bit block).
Buffers must be valid; overlapping input/output is not recommended due to different sizes.
Function does not report errors via return value; callers must ensure input lengths and parameters are valid to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: nist_keyunwrap16
functions.signature: int nist_keyunwrap16 (const void *ctx, nettle_cipher_func *decrypt, const uint8_t *iv, size_t cleartext_length, uint8_t *cleartext, const uint8_t *ciphertext);
functions.description: Unwraps key material using the NIST AES Key Wrap algorithm (RFC 3394), parameterized by a 16-byte block cipher provided via decrypt. Writes cleartext_length bytes of unwrapped data from a ciphertext buffer that should be cleartext_length + 8 bytes. Returns a status indicating integrity/authentication check success or failure (non-zero on success, zero on failure; exact values unspecified). The iv is the 8-byte initial value expected for the wrapped data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid cipher context matching decrypt.
decrypt must point to the corresponding 16-byte block cipher decryption function compatible with ctx.
iv must reference 8 bytes of initial value; it must match the one used for wrapping (default RFC 3394 IV is 0xA6*8; use of alternative IVs must match wrapping).
cleartext_length must be at least 8 and a multiple of 8.
ciphertext must contain cleartext_length + 8 bytes of input.
cleartext must have space for cleartext_length bytes of output.
Callers must check the return value and treat failure as authentication/integrity failure; output is invalid on failure.
Buffers must be valid; overlapping is not recommended due to different sizes.

functions.name: aes128_keywrap
functions.signature: void aes128_keywrap (struct aes128_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ciphertext_length, uint8_t *ciphertext, const uint8_t *cleartext);
functions.description: AES-128 specific wrapper for RFC 3394 key wrap. Uses ctx as the AES-128 encryption context to wrap cleartext into ciphertext_length bytes (cleartext_length + 8). Suitable for wrapping 8-byte multiple key material with AES-128.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for AES-128 encryption (e.g., via aes128_set_encrypt_key).
iv must reference 8 bytes (RFC 3394 initial value).
ciphertext_length must be at least 16 and a multiple of 8.
cleartext must contain ciphertext_length - 8 bytes of input (multiple of 8, >= 8).
ciphertext must have space for ciphertext_length bytes.
No return value; callers are responsible for providing valid parameters.

functions.name: aes192_keywrap
functions.signature: void aes192_keywrap (struct aes192_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ciphertext_length, uint8_t *ciphertext, const uint8_t *cleartext);
functions.description: AES-192 specific wrapper for RFC 3394 key wrap. Uses ctx as the AES-192 encryption context to wrap cleartext into ciphertext_length bytes (cleartext_length + 8).
requirements: ctx must be initialized for AES-192 encryption (e.g., via aes192_set_encrypt_key).
iv must reference 8 bytes (RFC 3394 initial value).
ciphertext_length must be at least 16 and a multiple of 8.
cleartext must contain ciphertext_length - 8 bytes of input (multiple of 8, >= 8).
ciphertext must have space for ciphertext_length bytes.
No return value; callers are responsible for providing valid parameters.

functions.name: aes256_keywrap
functions.signature: void aes256_keywrap (struct aes256_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *iv, size_t ciphertext_length, uint8_t *ciphertext, const uint8_t *cleartext);
functions.description: AES-256 specific wrapper for RFC 3394 key wrap. Uses ctx as the AES-256 encryption context to wrap cleartext into ciphertext_length bytes (cleartext_length + 8).
requirements: ctx must be initialized for AES-256 encryption (e.g., via aes256_set_encrypt_key).
iv must reference 8 bytes (RFC 3394 initial value).
ciphertext_length must be at least 16 and a multiple of 8.
cleartext must contain ciphertext_length - 8 bytes of input (multiple of 8, >= 8).
ciphertext must have space for ciphertext_length bytes.
No return value; callers are responsible for providing valid parameters.

functions.name: aes128_keyunwrap
functions.signature: int aes128_keyunwrap (struct aes128_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *iv, size_t cleartext_length, uint8_t *cleartext, const uint8_t *ciphertext);
functions.description: AES-128 specific unwrapping for RFC 3394 key wrap. Uses ctx as the AES-128 decryption context to unwrap cleartext_length bytes from ciphertext of size cleartext_length + 8. Returns a status indicating success (integrity check passed) or failure.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for AES-128 decryption (e.g., via aes128_set_decrypt_key).
iv must reference 8 bytes and must match the IV used during wrapping (RFC 3394 default is 0xA6*8 unless alternative used).
cleartext_length must be at least 8 and a multiple of 8.
ciphertext must contain cleartext_length + 8 bytes of input.
cleartext must have space for cleartext_length bytes of output.
Callers must check the return value; on failure, cleartext output must not be used.

functions.name: aes192_keyunwrap
functions.signature: int aes192_keyunwrap (struct aes192_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *iv, size_t cleartext_length, uint8_t *cleartext, const uint8_t *ciphertext);
functions.description: AES-192 specific unwrapping for RFC 3394 key wrap. Uses ctx as the AES-192 decryption context to unwrap cleartext_length bytes from ciphertext of size cleartext_length + 8. Returns a status indicating success or failure.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for AES-192 decryption (e.g., via aes192_set_decrypt_key).
iv must reference 8 bytes and must match the IV used during wrapping.
cleartext_length must be at least 8 and a multiple of 8.
ciphertext must contain cleartext_length + 8 bytes of input.

Callers must check the return value; on failure, output is invalid.

functions.name: aes256_keyunwrap
functions.signature: int aes256_keyunwrap (struct aes256_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *iv, size_t cleartext_length, uint8_t *cleartext, const uint8_t *ciphertext);
functions.description: AES-256 specific unwrapping for RFC 3394 key wrap. Uses ctx as the AES-256 decryption context to unwrap cleartext_length bytes from ciphertext of size cleartext_length + 8. Returns a status indicating success or failure.

iv must reference 8 bytes and must match the IV used during wrapping.
cleartext_length must be at least 8 and a multiple of 8.

functions.name: ocb_set_key
functions.signature: void ocb_set_key(struct ocb_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f);
functions.description: Initializes the OCB per-key subkeys (L values) using the provided block cipher context and its encrypt function. Call this once per key before setting nonces and processing data. Typical use: pass a pointer to an initialized block cipher context (e.g., AES) and its encrypt function.
requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer to struct ocb_key.
cipher must point to an initialized block cipher context compatible with f.
f must be a valid block-cipher encrypt function matching the type of cipher (nettle_cipher_func).
Must be called before ocb_set_nonce, ocb_update, ocb_encrypt/ocb_decrypt, and ocb_digest for a given key.

functions.name: ocb_set_nonce
functions.signature: void ocb_set_nonce(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t tag_length, size_t nonce_length, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Initializes or re-initializes an OCB context for a fresh message with the given nonce and desired tag length. After this call, you can supply associated data (ocb_update) and then encrypt/decrypt message data, and finally compute the authentication tag with ocb_digest.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to struct ocb_ctx.
cipher must point to an initialized block cipher context compatible with f (same key as used with ocb_set_key).
f must be the block-cipher encrypt function corresponding to cipher.
ocb_set_key must have been called for the key used with this ctx prior to message processing.
tag_length must be within the supported range [0, OCB_DIGEST_SIZE] (inferred from OCB_DIGEST_SIZE = 16).
nonce must point to nonce_length bytes of data.
nonce_length must be within the supported range [0, OCB_MAX_NONCE_SIZE] (inferred from OCB_MAX_NONCE_SIZE = 15).
Call before ocb_update/ocb_encrypt/ocb_decrypt for each new message.

functions.name: ocb_update
functions.signature: void ocb_update(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Processes associated data (AAD) for OCB authentication. This updates the AAD authentication state without producing output. Call after ocb_set_nonce and before or interleaved with encryption/decryption as needed.
requirements: ctx must be an initialized OCB context set up via ocb_set_nonce.
key must point to the precomputed OCB key (initialized via ocb_set_key).
cipher must point to an initialized block cipher context compatible with f and the provided key.
f must be the block-cipher encrypt function corresponding to cipher.
If length > 0, data must point to at least length bytes.
May be called zero or more times per message, after ocb_set_nonce and before ocb_digest.

functions.name: ocb_encrypt
functions.signature: void ocb_encrypt(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts plaintext to ciphertext while updating OCB authentication state. Use after ocb_set_nonce (and any ocb_update for AAD) and before ocb_digest.
requirements: ctx must be an OCB context initialized for the current message via ocb_set_nonce.
key must point to the OCB key initialized via ocb_set_key for the same cipher key.
cipher must point to an initialized block cipher context compatible with f and key.
f must be the block-cipher encrypt function corresponding to cipher.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of plaintext and dst must point to at least length bytes of writable buffer.
Call ocb_digest after finishing encryption to obtain the authentication tag.

functions.name: ocb_decrypt
functions.signature: void ocb_decrypt(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_key *key, const void *encrypt_ctx, nettle_cipher_func *encrypt, const void *decrypt_ctx, nettle_cipher_func *decrypt, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts ciphertext to plaintext while updating OCB authentication state. Requires both encrypt and decrypt cipher contexts/functions (per API design); use after ocb_set_nonce (and ocb_update for AAD) and before ocb_digest for tag verification.
requirements: ctx must be an OCB context initialized for the current message via ocb_set_nonce.
key must point to the OCB key initialized via ocb_set_key for the same cipher key.
encrypt_ctx and encrypt must be a valid block-cipher encryption context/function matching the key.
decrypt_ctx and decrypt must be a valid block-cipher decryption context/function matching the same key.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of ciphertext and dst must point to at least length bytes of writable buffer.
Caller must verify authenticity by computing and checking the tag (e.g., via ocb_digest) before using decrypted data; handle tag comparison securely.

functions.name: ocb_digest
functions.signature: void ocb_digest(const struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_key *key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t length, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes and outputs the OCB authentication tag for the current message state into digest. Call after processing all AAD (ocb_update) and message data (ocb_encrypt/ocb_decrypt).
requirements: ctx must be an OCB context that has been initialized via ocb_set_nonce and used to process all AAD and message data for this message.
key must point to the OCB key initialized via ocb_set_key for the same cipher key.
cipher must point to an initialized block cipher context compatible with f and key.
f must be the block-cipher encrypt function corresponding to cipher.
digest must point to at least length bytes of writable buffer.
length specifies the number of tag bytes to write and should match the tag_length set in ocb_set_nonce (inferred requirement).
Caller is responsible for comparing the generated tag to the expected tag in a secure (constant-time) manner.

functions.name: ocb_encrypt_message
functions.signature: void ocb_encrypt_message(const struct ocb_key *ocb_key, const void *cipher, nettle_cipher_func *f, size_t nlength, const uint8_t *nonce, size_t alength, const uint8_t *adata, size_t tlength, size_t clength, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: One-shot OCB encryption and authentication. Encrypts src plaintext of length clength, authenticates adata of length alength, using nonce of length nlength, and writes ciphertext followed by authentication tag of tlength bytes to dst.
requirements: ocb_key must point to an OCB key initialized via ocb_set_key (or an equivalent per-cipher setup) for the same cipher.
cipher must point to an initialized block cipher context compatible with f and ocb_key.
f must be the block-cipher encrypt function corresponding to cipher.
nonce must point to nlength bytes; nlength must be within [0, OCB_MAX_NONCE_SIZE] (inferred from constant).
tlength must be within [0, OCB_DIGEST_SIZE] (inferred from constant).
If alength > 0, adata must point to at least alength bytes.
If clength > 0, src must point to at least clength bytes of plaintext and dst must point to a buffer large enough for clength + tlength bytes.
Caller must ensure nonces are not reused with the same key.

functions.name: ocb_decrypt_message
functions.signature: int ocb_decrypt_message(const struct ocb_key *ocb_key, const void *encrypt_ctx, nettle_cipher_func *encrypt, const void *decrypt_ctx, nettle_cipher_func *decrypt, size_t nlength, const uint8_t *nonce, size_t alength, const uint8_t *adata, size_t tlength, size_t mlength, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: One-shot OCB decryption and authentication. Decrypts src ciphertext of length mlength with an appended tag of tlength bytes, authenticates adata of length alength, using nonce of length nlength, and writes plaintext to dst if authentication succeeds. Returns non-zero on success and zero on authentication failure (inferred from Nettle conventions).
requirements: ocb_key must point to an OCB key initialized via ocb_set_key for the same cipher.
encrypt_ctx/encrypt must be a valid block-cipher encryption context/function for the key; decrypt_ctx/decrypt must be a valid block-cipher decryption context/function for the same key.
nonce must point to nlength bytes; nlength must be within [0, OCB_MAX_NONCE_SIZE] (inferred from constant).
tlength must be within [0, OCB_DIGEST_SIZE] (inferred from constant).
If alength > 0, adata must point to at least alength bytes.
If mlength > 0, src must point to at least mlength + tlength bytes of input (ciphertext plus tag), and dst must point to at least mlength bytes of writable buffer (inferred from parameter names).
Caller must check the return value; on authentication failure (return 0), the contents of dst must not be used.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: void ocb_aes128_set_encrypt_key(struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *ocb, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes an OCB-AES-128 combined key: expands the AES-128 encryption key and precomputes OCB subkeys. Use this before setting nonces and processing data with the AES-128 specific APIs.
requirements: ocb must be a valid, writable pointer to struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key.
key must point to a 16-byte AES-128 key (inferred from AES-128).
Must be called before ocb_aes128_set_nonce, ocb_aes128_update, ocb_aes128_encrypt/decrypt, and ocb_aes128_digest.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_set_decrypt_key
functions.signature: void ocb_aes128_set_decrypt_key(struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *ocb, struct aes128_ctx *decrypt, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes the AES-128 decryption context corresponding to the given key and also prepares the OCB AES-128 encryption key structure. Use when decryption operations are needed.
requirements: ocb must point to a writable struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key (its encrypt subcontext will be set/used).
decrypt must point to a writable struct aes128_ctx to receive the expanded decryption key.
key must point to a 16-byte AES-128 key (inferred from AES-128).
Call before ocb_aes128_decrypt and before any decryption in one-shot decrypt_message.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_set_nonce
functions.signature: void ocb_aes128_set_nonce(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *key, size_t tag_length, size_t nonce_length, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Sets up an OCB context for AES-128 with the provided nonce and tag length, reinitializing per-message state. Use prior to AAD update and encryption/decryption.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable OCB context.
key must point to an initialized ocb_aes128_encrypt_key (set via ocb_aes128_set_encrypt_key/ocb_aes128_set_decrypt_key).
nonce must point to nonce_length bytes; nonce_length must be within [0, OCB_MAX_NONCE_SIZE] (inferred from constant).
tag_length must be within [0, OCB_DIGEST_SIZE] (inferred from constant).
Call before ocb_aes128_update/ocb_aes128_encrypt/ocb_aes128_decrypt.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_update
functions.signature: void ocb_aes128_update(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *key, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Processes associated data (AAD) for OCB with AES-128, updating authentication state without producing output.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for the current message via ocb_aes128_set_nonce.
key must point to an initialized ocb_aes128_encrypt_key.
If length > 0, data must point to at least length bytes.
May be called zero or more times per message before finalizing the tag.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_encrypt
functions.signature: void ocb_aes128_encrypt(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *key, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts plaintext to ciphertext using OCB with AES-128 while updating authentication state. Use after setting the nonce and any AAD updates, and before computing the tag.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for the current message via ocb_aes128_set_nonce.
key must point to an initialized ocb_aes128_encrypt_key.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of plaintext and dst must point to at least length bytes of writable buffer.
Call ocb_aes128_digest after finishing encryption to obtain the tag.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_decrypt
functions.signature: void ocb_aes128_decrypt(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *key, const struct aes128_ctx *decrypt, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts ciphertext to plaintext using OCB with AES-128 while updating authentication state. Requires the AES-128 decryption context.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for the current message via ocb_aes128_set_nonce.
key must point to an initialized ocb_aes128_encrypt_key (encrypt subkeys).
decrypt must point to an initialized AES-128 decryption context matching key.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of ciphertext and dst must point to at least length bytes of writable buffer.
Caller must verify authenticity by computing and checking the tag (e.g., via ocb_aes128_digest) before using decrypted data; handle tag comparison securely.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_digest
functions.signature: void ocb_aes128_digest(struct ocb_ctx *ctx, const struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *key, size_t length, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes and outputs the OCB authentication tag (AES-128 variant) into digest. Call after all AAD and message data have been processed.
requirements: ctx must be an OCB context that has been initialized via ocb_aes128_set_nonce and used to process all AAD and message data.
key must point to an initialized ocb_aes128_encrypt_key.
digest must point to at least length bytes of writable buffer.
length is the requested tag size and should be consistent with the tag length used for this message (inferred).
Caller is responsible for securely comparing the tag with the expected value.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_encrypt_message
functions.signature: void ocb_aes128_encrypt_message(const struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *key, size_t nlength, const uint8_t *nonce, size_t alength, const uint8_t *adata, size_t tlength, size_t clength, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: One-shot OCB-AES-128 encryption and authentication. Encrypts src plaintext of length clength, authenticates adata of length alength with nonce of length nlength, and writes ciphertext followed by a tag of tlength bytes to dst.
requirements: key must point to an initialized ocb_aes128_encrypt_key (via ocb_aes128_set_encrypt_key).
nonce must point to nlength bytes; nlength must be within [0, OCB_MAX_NONCE_SIZE] (inferred).
tlength must be within [0, OCB_DIGEST_SIZE] (inferred).
If alength > 0, adata must point to at least alength bytes.
If clength > 0, src must point to at least clength bytes of plaintext and dst must point to a buffer large enough for clength + tlength bytes.
Caller must ensure nonces are not reused with the same key.

functions.name: ocb_aes128_decrypt_message
functions.signature: int ocb_aes128_decrypt_message(const struct ocb_aes128_encrypt_key *key, const struct aes128_ctx *decrypt, size_t nlength, const uint8_t *nonce, size_t alength, const uint8_t *adata, size_t tlength, size_t mlength, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: One-shot OCB-AES-128 decryption and authentication. Decrypts src input consisting of mlength bytes of ciphertext plus a tlength-byte tag, authenticates adata, and writes plaintext to dst if authentication succeeds. Returns non-zero on success and zero on authentication failure (inferred from Nettle conventions).
requirements: key must point to an initialized ocb_aes128_encrypt_key (same key used for encryption).
decrypt must point to an initialized AES-128 decryption context matching key.
nonce must point to nlength bytes; nlength must be within [0, OCB_MAX_NONCE_SIZE] (inferred).
tlength must be within [0, OCB_DIGEST_SIZE] (inferred).
If alength > 0, adata must point to at least alength bytes.
If mlength > 0, src must point to at least mlength + tlength bytes (ciphertext plus tag), and dst must point to at least mlength bytes of writable buffer (inferred from parameter names).
Caller must check the return value; on authentication failure (return 0), the contents of dst must not be used.

functions.name: pbkdf2
functions.signature: void pbkdf2(void *mac_ctx, nettle_hash_update_func *update, nettle_hash_digest_func *digest, size_t digest_size, unsigned iterations, size_t salt_length, const uint8_t *salt, size_t length, uint8_t *dst);
functions.description: Generic PBKDF2 key derivation using a caller-supplied PRF (typically HMAC over a hash). The caller provides a MAC/hash context and compatible update/digest function pointers along with the PRF output size; the function derives ‘length’ bytes of keying material into ‘dst’ using the given salt and iteration count. Use this when you need PBKDF2 with a custom PRF supported by Nettle’s hash interface. Returns no status; fills dst deterministically based on inputs.
requirements: mac_ctx must be a valid and initialized context for the PRF corresponding to the provided update and digest functions.
update must point to a function compatible with nettle_hash_update_func for the mac_ctx type.
digest must point to a function compatible with nettle_hash_digest_func for the mac_ctx type.
digest_size must equal the output size (in bytes) of the provided PRF/digest function.
iterations must be >= 1 (PBKDF2 requires at least one iteration).
If salt_length > 0, salt must point to at least salt_length readable bytes; salt may be NULL only if salt_length is 0.
dst must point to a buffer of at least ‘length’ writable bytes.
length may be 0 to derive an empty key; in that case dst is not dereferenced.
The function performs no memory allocation and provides no error reporting; callers must ensure arguments are valid to avoid undefined behavior.
If mac_ctx is shared across threads or calls, external synchronization is required; the function may mutate mac_ctx via update/digest.

functions.name: pkcs1_encrypt
functions.signature: int pkcs1_encrypt(size_t key_size, void *random_ctx, nettle_random_func *random, size_t length, const uint8_t *message, mpz_t m);
functions.description: Performs PKCS#1 v1.5 RSA encryption padding (EME-PKCS1-v1_5) on the input message and converts the result to an integer representative m suitable for RSA public-key operation. The key_size is the RSA modulus size in bytes. A caller-supplied RNG (random_ctx, random) is used to generate the nonzero padding bytes. Returns a success indicator (non-zero on success, zero on failure is typical in Nettle). Use when preparing plaintext for RSA encryption with a modulus of key_size bytes.
requirements: key_size must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
message must point to length bytes of plaintext to be padded.
length must satisfy the EME-PKCS1-v1_5 constraint: length <= key_size - 11 (at least 8 bytes of nonzero padding plus 3 marker bytes).
random must be a valid function pointer and random_ctx must be suitable for it; the RNG must provide cryptographically strong, nonzero bytes for padding.
m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written to contain the encoded integer representative in the interval [0, n-1] where n has size key_size bytes.
The function returns an int status; callers should check the return value and not use m on failure.
The modulus corresponding to key_size must be large enough to accommodate the encoded block; otherwise the function fails.

functions.name: pkcs1_decrypt
functions.signature: int pkcs1_decrypt(size_t key_size, const mpz_t m, size_t *length, uint8_t *message);
functions.description: Removes PKCS#1 v1.5 RSA encryption padding (EME-PKCS1-v1_5) from an integer representative m (result of RSA private-key operation) for a key of key_size bytes, writing the recovered plaintext into message. The length parameter is used for in/out sizing: on input, *length provides the capacity of message; on output, *length is set to the actual plaintext length. Returns a success indicator (non-zero on success, zero on failure is typical in Nettle). Use after performing RSA private-key operation to obtain the original plaintext.
requirements: key_size must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes) matching the RSA key used to produce m.
m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t containing the RSA result to be unpadded (typically the raw RSA decryption output).
message must point to writable storage with capacity given by *length on input.
On input, *length must be set to the available size of message in bytes; on output, *length is set to the actual plaintext length.
The buffer capacity provided via *length must be at least key_size - 11 bytes to accommodate the maximum possible plaintext size under PKCS#1 v1.5.
The function validates PKCS#1 v1.5 structure; callers must check the return value and treat failure as invalid padding or size mismatch.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_digest_encode
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_digest_encode(mpz_t m, size_t key_size, size_t di_length, const uint8_t *digest_info);
functions.description: Encodes a complete ASN.1 DigestInfo (algorithm identifier + digest) into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block for an RSA modulus of key_size bytes, and writes the resulting integer representative to m. Use this when you already have a DER-encoded DigestInfo blob and need to prepare it for RSA signature (or verification). Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
key_size must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
digest_info must point to a di_length-byte DER-encoded DigestInfo structure for the intended hash algorithm.
The encoded block size must fit the modulus size: di_length must satisfy di_length <= key_size - 11 (per EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5).
Callers must check the return value and not use m on failure.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_md5_encode
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_md5_encode(mpz_t m, size_t length, struct md5_ctx *hash);
functions.description: Computes the MD5 digest from the provided md5_ctx and encodes the corresponding ASN.1 DigestInfo into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block of size length bytes, storing the integer representative in m. Intended for preparing RSA signatures using MD5 (legacy). Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
length must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).

hash must point to a valid MD5 context containing the message hash state suitable for extracting a 16-byte MD5 digest (exact requirements on finalization are not documented here; the context must represent the desired digest).
The EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 size constraint applies: the MD5 DigestInfo (fixed size) must fit within length - 11 bytes.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_md5_encode_digest
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_md5_encode_digest(mpz_t m, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Encodes a raw 16-byte MD5 digest into the MD5 ASN.1 DigestInfo and then into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block for an RSA modulus of length bytes, storing the integer representative in m. Use when you already have the MD5 digest. Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
length must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
digest must point to 16 bytes containing the MD5 hash of the message.
The EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 size constraint applies: the resulting DigestInfo must fit within length - 11 bytes.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_sha1_encode
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_sha1_encode(mpz_t m, size_t length, struct sha1_ctx *hash);
functions.description: Computes the SHA-1 digest from the provided sha1_ctx and encodes the corresponding ASN.1 DigestInfo into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block of size length bytes, storing the integer representative in m. Intended for preparing RSA signatures using SHA-1 (legacy). Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
length must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
hash must point to a valid SHA-1 context containing the message hash state suitable for extracting a 20-byte digest (exact finalization semantics not documented here).
The EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 size constraint applies: the SHA-1 DigestInfo must fit within length - 11 bytes.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_sha1_encode_digest
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_sha1_encode_digest(mpz_t m, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Encodes a raw 20-byte SHA-1 digest into the SHA-1 ASN.1 DigestInfo and then into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block for an RSA modulus of length bytes, storing the integer representative in m. Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
length must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
digest must point to 20 bytes containing the SHA-1 hash of the message.
The EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 size constraint applies: the resulting DigestInfo must fit within length - 11 bytes.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_sha256_encode
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_sha256_encode(mpz_t m, size_t length, struct sha256_ctx *hash);
functions.description: Computes the SHA-256 digest from the provided sha256_ctx and encodes the corresponding ASN.1 DigestInfo into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block of size length bytes, storing the integer representative in m. Intended for RSA signatures using SHA-256. Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
length must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
hash must point to a valid SHA-256 context containing the message hash state suitable for extracting a 32-byte digest (exact finalization semantics not documented here).
The EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 size constraint applies: the SHA-256 DigestInfo must fit within length - 11 bytes.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_sha256_encode_digest
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_sha256_encode_digest(mpz_t m, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Encodes a raw 32-byte SHA-256 digest into the SHA-256 ASN.1 DigestInfo and then into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block for an RSA modulus of length bytes, storing the integer representative in m. Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
length must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
digest must point to 32 bytes containing the SHA-256 hash of the message.
The EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 size constraint applies: the resulting DigestInfo must fit within length - 11 bytes.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_sha512_encode
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_sha512_encode(mpz_t m, size_t length, struct sha512_ctx *hash);
functions.description: Computes the SHA-512 digest from the provided sha512_ctx and encodes the corresponding ASN.1 DigestInfo into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block of size length bytes, storing the integer representative in m. Intended for RSA signatures using SHA-512. Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
length must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
hash must point to a valid SHA-512 context containing the message hash state suitable for extracting a 64-byte digest (exact finalization semantics not documented here).
The EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 size constraint applies: the SHA-512 DigestInfo must fit within length - 11 bytes.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: pkcs1_rsa_sha512_encode_digest
functions.signature: int pkcs1_rsa_sha512_encode_digest(mpz_t m, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Encodes a raw 64-byte SHA-512 digest into the SHA-512 ASN.1 DigestInfo and then into an EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 padded block for an RSA modulus of length bytes, storing the integer representative in m. Returns a success indicator.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and will be written with the encoded representative.
length must be the RSA modulus size in octets (bytes).
digest must point to 64 bytes containing the SHA-512 hash of the message.
The EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 size constraint applies: the resulting DigestInfo must fit within length - 11 bytes.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: poly1305_aes_set_key
functions.signature: void poly1305_aes_set_key(struct poly1305_aes_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Poly1305-AES message authentication context with the given 32-byte key. As documented, this also initializes the internal nonce to zero so that the first message uses nonce=0 unless explicitly set later. Typical usage: call once to initialize a context, optionally set a nonce, then feed message data via poly1305_aes_update and finalize with poly1305_aes_digest.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct poly1305_aes_ctx.
key must point to at least POLY1305_AES_KEY_SIZE (32) bytes.
Call this function before calling poly1305_aes_update or poly1305_aes_digest on the context.
As documented, this call initializes the internal nonce to zero.
Inferred from Poly1305-AES design: for security, each message processed under a given key must use a unique nonce.

functions.name: poly1305_aes_set_nonce
functions.signature: void poly1305_aes_set_nonce(struct poly1305_aes_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Sets the 16-byte nonce for the next message to be authenticated with the Poly1305-AES context. The header notes this is optional; if not used, messages will use incrementing nonces starting from zero (after key setup). Use this to supply an explicit nonce value for the next message.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct poly1305_aes_ctx previously initialized with poly1305_aes_set_key.
nonce must point to at least POLY1305_AES_NONCE_SIZE (16) bytes.
If not called, the context uses incrementing nonces starting from zero (as documented).
Inferred from Poly1305-AES design: nonces must be unique per message for a given key.
Effective timing: the set nonce applies to the next authentication operation that is finalized by poly1305_aes_digest.

functions.name: poly1305_aes_update
functions.signature: void poly1305_aes_update(struct poly1305_aes_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds message data into the current Poly1305-AES computation. Can be called zero or more times to process a message before finalizing with poly1305_aes_digest. This update routine is the active variant for the provided AES-based poly1305 implementation.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct poly1305_aes_ctx initialized with poly1305_aes_set_key (and optionally poly1305_aes_set_nonce).
If length > 0, data must point to at least length bytes readable memory; if length == 0, data may be NULL.
Call poly1305_aes_digest to finalize the current message after all updates; do not call digest before any update unless finalizing an empty message is intended.
Data may be supplied in multiple calls; ordering is significant and preserved.

functions.name: poly1305_aes_digest
functions.signature: void poly1305_aes_digest(struct poly1305_aes_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the current Poly1305-AES computation and writes the 16-byte authentication tag to the supplied buffer. As documented, calling this also increments the internal nonce for the next message. After digest, new message data (if any) will be associated with the incremented nonce unless a new nonce is set explicitly.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a struct poly1305_aes_ctx initialized with poly1305_aes_set_key.
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least POLY1305_AES_DIGEST_SIZE (16) bytes.
Must be called after supplying all message data via poly1305_aes_update (possibly none for an empty message).
As documented, this call increments the internal nonce for subsequent messages.
If explicit nonces are required by the application, call poly1305_aes_set_nonce before the next message; otherwise the auto-incremented nonce will be used.
Inferred from Poly1305-AES design: do not reuse a nonce for different messages under the same key.

functions.name: pss_encode_mgf1
functions.signature: int pss_encode_mgf1(mpz_t m, size_t bits, const struct nettle_hash *hash, size_t salt_length, const uint8_t *salt, const uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Encodes a message hash using PKCS#1 v2.1 RSA-PSS (EMSA-PSS-ENCODE) with MGF1. On success, writes the encoded message representative into m to match an RSA modulus size of ‘bits’. Typical usage: compute the message digest with the selected hash algorithm, optionally provide a salt (salt_length bytes), then call this function before RSA private-key operation to produce the PSS-encoded block. Returns a status integer (nonzero on success, zero on failure in Nettle conventions). Specific return semantics are not documented in this header; details such as failure modes are inferred from standard Nettle patterns and the function name.
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t and is used as an output parameter to receive the encoded message representative.

bits must be the target bit length of the RSA modulus (emBits); it must be large enough for PSS with the selected hash and salt length (per RFC 3447, emLen >= hLen + sLen + 2). If too small, the function will fail.
hash must be a valid, initialized pointer to a nettle_hash descriptor; its digest size determines the expected length of ‘digest’.
digest must point to exactly hash->digest_size bytes containing the message hash to be encoded.
salt may be NULL only if salt_length is zero; otherwise it must point to at least salt_length bytes.
The resulting encoded value m will satisfy masking rules for emBits; callers should ensure the RSA modulus size corresponds to ‘bits’.
Return value handling: callers must check the int return value and treat a zero return as an encoding failure (reason not specified here).

functions.name: pss_verify_mgf1
functions.signature: int pss_verify_mgf1(const mpz_t m, size_t bits, const struct nettle_hash *hash, size_t salt_length, const uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Verifies a PKCS#1 v2.1 RSA-PSS encoding (EMSA-PSS-VERIFY) with MGF1. Given an encoded message representative m (typically recovered by RSA public-key operation), the modulus bit size ‘bits’, the hash algorithm, an expected salt length, and the message digest, checks whether m is a valid PSS encoding of ‘digest’. Returns a status integer (nonzero on successful verification, zero on failure, inferred from Nettle conventions).
requirements: m must be an initialized GMP mpz_t containing the candidate encoded message representative (input).
bits must match the bit length of the RSA modulus used to produce m (emBits). If inconsistent or too small for the given parameters, verification fails.
hash must be a valid, initialized pointer to a nettle_hash descriptor; its digest size determines the expected length of ‘digest’.
digest must point to exactly hash->digest_size bytes containing the message hash that should have been encoded.
salt_length specifies the expected salt length; verification will fail if the encoding implies a different salt length (per PSS).
The leftmost padding/mask bits implied by emBits are checked; callers must pass the same ‘bits’ used during encoding.
Return value handling: callers must check the int return value and treat a zero return as verification failure.

functions.name: ripemd160_init
functions.signature: void ripemd160_init(struct ripemd160_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a RIPEMD-160 hashing context. Call this before supplying any input with ripemd160_update and before producing the final hash with ripemd160_digest. Note: The header defines macros mapping this symbol to nettle_ripemd160_init for name mangling.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and point to a writable struct ripemd160_ctx instance.
This function must be called before ripemd160_update or ripemd160_digest are used with the same ctx.
No error is returned; callers should not expect error codes or status indicators.

functions.name: ripemd160_update
functions.signature: void ripemd160_update(struct ripemd160_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds input bytes into an initialized RIPEMD-160 context. May be called repeatedly to process data in chunks before finalizing with ripemd160_digest. Input is not modified. Note: The header defines macros mapping this symbol to nettle_ripemd160_update for name mangling.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and must have been initialized by ripemd160_init before the first update.
length is the number of bytes to process; if length > 0, data must be non-null and point to at least length readable bytes.
If length == 0, the function performs no update; in that case data may be null.
No error is returned; callers should not expect error codes or status indicators.

functions.name: ripemd160_digest
functions.signature: void ripemd160_digest(struct ripemd160_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the RIPEMD-160 computation for the provided context and writes the 20-byte message digest to the output buffer. Typically called after all ripemd160_update calls. The header does not specify whether the context is reset or remains usable after this call; callers should not rely on either behavior without consulting implementation or higher-level docs. Note: The header defines macros mapping this symbol to nettle_ripemd160_digest for name mangling.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and must have been initialized with ripemd160_init, typically after all desired ripemd160_update calls.
digest must be non-null and point to at least RIPEMD160_DIGEST_SIZE (20) writable bytes.
No error is returned; callers should not expect error codes or status indicators.

functions.name: rsa_public_key_init
functions.signature: void rsa_public_key_init(struct rsa_public_key *key);
functions.description: Initializes an rsa_public_key by calling mpz_init on its big-integer fields and resetting size. Use before setting key->n and key->e or calling prepare/verify/encrypt.
requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer
Call exactly once before first use of this rsa_public_key and before calling rsa_public_key_clear on it

functions.name: rsa_public_key_clear
functions.signature: void rsa_public_key_clear(struct rsa_public_key *key);
functions.description: Clears an initialized rsa_public_key, calling mpz_clear on its big-integer fields to free associated memory.
requirements: key must have been previously initialized with rsa_public_key_init
Do not use the key after clearing unless re-initialized

functions.name: rsa_public_key_prepare
functions.signature: int rsa_public_key_prepare(struct rsa_public_key *key);
functions.description: Prepares a public key for use (computes and sets derived fields such as size). Returns nonzero on success, zero on invalid key.
requirements: key must be initialized with rsa_public_key_init
key->n and key->e must be set to valid RSA parameters before calling
The modulus size must meet the library’s minimums (e.g., RSA_MINIMUM_N_BITS)

functions.name: rsa_private_key_init
functions.signature: void rsa_private_key_init(struct rsa_private_key *key);
functions.description: Initializes an rsa_private_key by calling mpz_init on all big-integer fields and resetting size.
requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer
Call exactly once before first use and before rsa_private_key_clear

functions.name: rsa_private_key_clear
functions.signature: void rsa_private_key_clear(struct rsa_private_key *key);
functions.description: Clears an initialized rsa_private_key, calling mpz_clear on all big-integer fields.
requirements: key must have been previously initialized with rsa_private_key_init
Do not use the key after clearing unless re-initialized

functions.name: rsa_private_key_prepare
functions.signature: int rsa_private_key_prepare(struct rsa_private_key *key);
functions.description: Prepares a private key for use (computes and validates derived CRT values and sets size). Returns nonzero on success.
requirements: key must be initialized with rsa_private_key_init
The key’s components (at least p, q, and exponents or d/a/b/c as applicable) must be set before calling
The modulus size must meet library minimums

functions.name: rsa_pkcs1_sign
functions.signature: int rsa_pkcs1_sign(const struct rsa_private_key *key, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest_info, mpz_t s);
functions.description: Signs a PKCS#1 v1.5 DigestInfo blob using the RSA private key, producing a signature as a big integer s. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (e.g., too long for key).
requirements: key must be an initialized and prepared RSA private key
digest_info must point to a DER-encoded DigestInfo value of size length (hash OID + digest)
length must be compatible with key size after PKCS#1 v1.5 padding
s must be an initialized mpz_t ready to receive the signature

functions.name: rsa_pkcs1_sign_tr
functions.signature: int rsa_pkcs1_sign_tr(const struct rsa_public_key *pub, const struct rsa_private_key *key, void *random_ctx, nettle_random_func *random, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest_info, mpz_t s);

functions.name: rsa_pkcs1_verify
functions.signature: int rsa_pkcs1_verify(const struct rsa_public_key *key, size_t length, const uint8_t *digest_info, const mpz_t signature);

signature must be a valid mpz_t within [0, n) for the key

functions.name: salsa20_128_set_key
functions.signature: void salsa20_128_set_key(struct salsa20_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Salsa20 context with a 128-bit (16-byte) key. Use before setting the nonce and calling salsa20_crypt to encrypt/decrypt data. This sets up internal state for the 16-byte key variant (the 16-byte key is internally duplicated to fill the state).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable struct salsa20_ctx.
key must point to at least 16 bytes of key material.
This function must be called before salsa20_set_nonce and any call to salsa20_crypt/salsa20r12_crypt using this context.
Key length is fixed at 16 bytes for this function; do not pass longer/shorter keys.
Security requirement (inferred from Salsa20 semantics): never reuse the same (key, nonce) pair across messages.

functions.name: salsa20_256_set_key
functions.signature: void salsa20_256_set_key(struct salsa20_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Salsa20 context with a 256-bit (32-byte) key. Use before setting the nonce and calling salsa20_crypt to encrypt/decrypt data. This sets up internal state for the 32-byte key variant.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable struct salsa20_ctx.
key must point to at least 32 bytes of key material.
This function must be called before salsa20_set_nonce and any call to salsa20_crypt/salsa20r12_crypt using this context.
Key length is fixed at 32 bytes for this function; do not pass longer/shorter keys.
Security requirement (inferred from Salsa20 semantics): never reuse the same (key, nonce) pair across messages.

functions.name: salsa20_set_key
functions.signature: void salsa20_set_key(struct salsa20_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Salsa20 context with either a 128-bit (16-byte) or 256-bit (32-byte) key, depending on the specified length. Use this variant when the key size is selected at runtime. After setting the key, set the nonce and then call salsa20_crypt to encrypt/decrypt.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable struct salsa20_ctx.
key must point to at least length bytes of key material.
length must be exactly 16 or 32; other lengths are not supported (16-byte keys are internally duplicated to fill the state).
This function must be called before salsa20_set_nonce and any call to salsa20_crypt/salsa20r12_crypt using this context.
Security requirement (inferred from Salsa20 semantics): never reuse the same (key, nonce) pair across messages.

functions.name: salsa20_set_nonce
functions.signature: void salsa20_set_nonce(struct salsa20_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Sets the 64-bit (8-byte) nonce/IV in an initialized Salsa20 context. Call after setting the key and before encrypting/decrypting. Can be called again with a new nonce to process independent messages under the same key.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct salsa20_ctx that has had a key set via one of the salsa20_*_set_key functions.
nonce must point to at least 8 bytes (SALSA20_NONCE_SIZE).
Nonce size is fixed at 8 bytes; do not pass longer/shorter nonces.
Security requirement (inferred from Salsa20 semantics): never reuse the same nonce with the same key across different messages.

functions.name: salsa20_crypt
functions.signature: void salsa20_crypt(struct salsa20_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts data using Salsa20 with the context’s current key and nonce. As a stream cipher, encryption and decryption are the same operation (XOR with generated keystream). Processes length bytes from src into dst.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct salsa20_ctx initialized with a key and a nonce.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of input and dst must point to at least length bytes of writable output.
dst and src may refer to the same buffer for in-place operation (inferred from typical stream-cipher API patterns).
The function does not return a status; callers should ensure parameters are valid to avoid undefined behavior.
Security requirement (inferred): do not reuse the same (key, nonce) pair across different plaintexts; doing so compromises confidentiality.

functions.name: salsa20r12_crypt
functions.signature: void salsa20r12_crypt(struct salsa20_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts data using the 12-round (reduced-round) variant of Salsa20 with the context’s current key and nonce. As with salsa20_crypt, the operation is XOR with keystream; this variant may be faster but has different security margins.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct salsa20_ctx initialized with a key and a nonce (using the standard key/nonce setters).
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of input and dst must point to at least length bytes of writable output.
dst and src may refer to the same buffer for in-place operation (inferred from typical stream-cipher API patterns).
The function does not return a status; callers should ensure parameters are valid to avoid undefined behavior.

Security requirement (inferred): do not reuse the same (key, nonce) pair across different plaintexts; doing so compromises confidentiality. Also note this is a reduced-round variant with different security margins compared to full Salsa20.

functions.name: serpent_set_key
functions.signature: void serpent_set_key(struct serpent_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a serpent_ctx with a user-supplied key for the Serpent 128-bit block cipher. Supports variable key sizes within the Serpent-allowed range. Call this once before using serpent_encrypt or serpent_decrypt with the same context. Exact handling of key lengths that are not 32 bytes is library-defined; based on header comments, keys from 16 to 32 bytes are accepted.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory for a serpent_ctx.
key must point to at least length bytes of readable memory (non-null if length > 0).
length must be in bytes and within [SERPENT_MIN_KEY_SIZE (16), SERPENT_MAX_KEY_SIZE (32)], inclusive.
The context must be initialized by this function before any call to serpent_encrypt or serpent_decrypt that uses this ctx.
This function does not report errors via return value; callers must ensure inputs meet the stated constraints.

functions.name: serpent128_set_key
functions.signature: void serpent128_set_key(struct serpent_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a serpent_ctx with a 128-bit (16-byte) key for the Serpent cipher. Use this when the key size is exactly 128 bits. Must be called before encryption/decryption with this context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory for a serpent_ctx.
key must point to at least SERPENT128_KEY_SIZE (16) bytes of readable memory (non-null).
The context must be initialized by this function (or another serpent*_set_key) before any call to serpent_encrypt or serpent_decrypt that uses this ctx.
This function does not report errors via return value; callers must ensure inputs meet the stated constraints.

functions.name: serpent192_set_key
functions.signature: void serpent192_set_key(struct serpent_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a serpent_ctx with a 192-bit (24-byte) key for the Serpent cipher. Use this for exactly 192-bit keys. Must be called before encryption/decryption with this context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory for a serpent_ctx.
key must point to at least SERPENT192_KEY_SIZE (24) bytes of readable memory (non-null).
The context must be initialized by this function (or another serpent*_set_key) before any call to serpent_encrypt or serpent_decrypt that uses this ctx.
This function does not report errors via return value; callers must ensure inputs meet the stated constraints.

functions.name: serpent256_set_key
functions.signature: void serpent256_set_key(struct serpent_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a serpent_ctx with a 256-bit (32-byte) key for the Serpent cipher. This is the full-size Serpent key. Must be called before encryption/decryption with this context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory for a serpent_ctx.
key must point to at least SERPENT256_KEY_SIZE (32) bytes of readable memory (non-null).
The context must be initialized by this function (or another serpent*_set_key) before any call to serpent_encrypt or serpent_decrypt that uses this ctx.
This function does not report errors via return value; callers must ensure inputs meet the stated constraints.

functions.name: serpent_encrypt
functions.signature: void serpent_encrypt(const struct serpent_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts data using the Serpent block cipher in ECB-like multi-block form: processes length bytes from src into dst using the provided serpent_ctx key schedule. The buffer length must be a multiple of the 16-byte block size. Call a serpent*_set_key function first to initialize ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized serpent_ctx previously set with serpent_set_key/serpent128_set_key/serpent192_set_key/serpent256_set_key.
length must be in bytes and a multiple of SERPENT_BLOCK_SIZE (16).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory (non-null if length > 0).
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory (non-null if length > 0).
This function returns void and provides no error reporting; callers must satisfy preconditions to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: serpent_decrypt
functions.signature: void serpent_decrypt(const struct serpent_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts data using the Serpent block cipher in ECB-like multi-block form: processes length bytes from src into dst using the provided serpent_ctx key schedule. The buffer length must be a multiple of the 16-byte block size. Call a serpent*_set_key function first to initialize ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized serpent_ctx previously set with serpent_set_key/serpent128_set_key/serpent192_set_key/serpent256_set_key.
length must be in bytes and a multiple of SERPENT_BLOCK_SIZE (16).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory (non-null if length > 0).
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory (non-null if length > 0).
This function returns void and provides no error reporting; callers must satisfy preconditions to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: sexp_iterator_first
functions.signature: int sexp_iterator_first(struct sexp_iterator *iterator, size_t length, const uint8_t *input);
functions.description: Initializes an s-expression iterator over a read-only buffer. On success, the iterator is positioned at the first expression. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. The iterator references the provided input buffer, so the buffer must remain valid while the iterator is used.
requirements: iterator must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for initialization
input must point to a buffer of at least length bytes when length > 0 (the iterator stores pointers into it)
the input buffer’s lifetime must outlive all uses of the iterator (iterator keeps pointers into input)
callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure

functions.name: sexp_transport_iterator_first
