functions.signature: int sexp_transport_iterator_first(struct sexp_iterator *iterator, size_t length, uint8_t *input);
functions.description: Initializes an s-expression iterator over a buffer encoded using the transport format. The input is decoded in place (the function may modify the buffer). On success, the iterator is positioned at the first decoded expression. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: iterator must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for initialization
input must be a non-NULL, writable buffer of at least length bytes; the function may modify its contents in place
the (now-decoded) input buffer must remain valid while the iterator is used (iterator keeps pointers into it)
callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure

functions.name: sexp_iterator_next
functions.signature: int sexp_iterator_next(struct sexp_iterator *iterator);
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next subexpression at the current level. Returns 1 on success, 0 when there is no next element or on failure.
requirements: iterator must have been successfully initialized (e.g., by sexp_iterator_first or sexp_transport_iterator_first) and must remain valid
callers must check the return value to detect end-of-sequence or errors

functions.name: sexp_iterator_enter_list
functions.signature: int sexp_iterator_enter_list(struct sexp_iterator *iterator);
functions.description: Enters the current list element, so subsequent iteration is over its elements. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. The current element must be a list.
requirements: iterator must be initialized and currently positioned at a list element
if the current element is not a list, the function fails (returns 0)
callers must check the return value

functions.name: sexp_iterator_exit_list
functions.signature: int sexp_iterator_exit_list(struct sexp_iterator *iterator);
functions.description: Skips the remaining elements of the current list and positions the iterator after that list. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: iterator must be initialized and currently inside a list context
callers must check the return value

functions.name: sexp_iterator_subexpr
functions.signature: const uint8_t * sexp_iterator_subexpr(struct sexp_iterator *iterator, size_t *length);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the start of the current subexpression and stores its length at length. This operation implies a move to the next element (it consumes the current subexpression). Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: iterator must be initialized and positioned at a valid subexpression
length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the subexpression length
the returned pointer refers into the original input buffer and remains valid only as long as that buffer remains valid
callers must check the return value for NULL to detect failure

functions.name: sexp_iterator_get_uint32
functions.signature: int sexp_iterator_get_uint32(struct sexp_iterator *iterator, uint32_t *x);
functions.description: Parses the current element as a non-negative 32-bit unsigned integer and stores the value in x. Advances the iterator on success. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: iterator must be initialized and positioned at an element representing a non-negative integer that fits in uint32_t
x must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the parsed value
callers must check the return value; on failure, x is not modified

functions.name: sexp_iterator_check_type
functions.signature: int sexp_iterator_check_type(struct sexp_iterator *iterator, const char *type);
functions.description: Checks that the current expression is a list whose first element (the "type" tag) matches the provided ASCII token type, i.e., of the form (type ...). Returns 1 on match, 0 otherwise.
requirements: iterator must be initialized and positioned at a list expression
type must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the expected tag
callers must check the return value to verify the type match

functions.name: sexp_iterator_check_types
functions.signature: const char * sexp_iterator_check_types(struct sexp_iterator *iterator, unsigned ntypes, const char * const *types);
functions.description: Checks that the current expression is a list whose first element matches one of the provided type tags. On success, returns a pointer to the matching tag string; on failure, returns NULL. The format is expected to be (type ...).
requirements: iterator must be initialized and positioned at a list expression
types must point to an array of ntypes NUL-terminated strings; ntypes specifies the number of entries
callers must check for a NULL return to detect no match

functions.name: sexp_iterator_assoc
functions.signature: int sexp_iterator_assoc(struct sexp_iterator *iterator, unsigned nkeys, const char * const *keys, struct sexp_iterator *values);
functions.description: Looks up an element in the current list by key, where elements have the form (key rest...). If a matching key is found, initializes values to point at the start of rest and exits the current list. Returns 1 if a matching key was found and values initialized, 0 otherwise.
requirements: iterator must be initialized and currently positioned at a list
keys must point to an array of nkeys NUL-terminated strings naming the recognized keys
values must be a non-NULL pointer to a sexp_iterator to receive the sub-iterator for the value part
on success, the function exits the current list; callers should not continue iterating the old list without re-establishing context
callers must check the return value

functions.name: sexp_format
functions.signature: size_t sexp_format(struct nettle_buffer *buffer, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Formats an s-expression into buffer according to a mini-language. Returns the number of output characters, or 0 on out-of-memory. If buffer == NULL, computes the required length without producing output. Supported specifiers: %s (size_t length, const uint8_t *data), %t (optional display type: size_t display_length, const uint8_t *display; display == NULL ⇒ none), %i (non-negative uint32_t), %b (non-negative mpz_t), %l (literal string: size_t length, const uint8_t *data), %( and %) to inject unbalanced parentheses. Modifier %0 changes %s/%t/%l to accept a single NUL-terminated const uint8_t * without a length.
requirements: buffer may be NULL to request length-only; otherwise must point to an initialized nettle_buffer with sufficient capacity or growable semantics per nettle_buffer
format must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string with well-formed parentheses unless intentionally unbalanced using %( and %)
varargs must exactly match the format specifiers in type and order
for %s and %l: provide (size_t length, const uint8_t *data) unless %0 is used; data must be valid for length bytes
for %t: provide (size_t display_length, const uint8_t *display) or display == NULL to indicate no display; with %0, provide only (const uint8_t *display) NUL-terminated
for %i: argument must be a non-negative uint32_t; values are encoded as small integers
for %b: argument must be a non-negative mpz_t initialized by GMP
callers must check the return value: 0 indicates failure (out-of-memory)

functions.name: sexp_vformat
functions.signature: size_t sexp_vformat(struct nettle_buffer *buffer, const char *format, va_list args);
functions.description: va_list variant of sexp_format. Formats according to the same mini-language using an existing va_list. Returns the number of output characters, or 0 on out-of-memory. If buffer == NULL, computes the required length only.
requirements: args must be an initialized va_list whose contents match the format specifiers exactly
all requirements of sexp_format regarding buffer, format, argument types, and value constraints also apply
callers must check the return value: 0 indicates failure (out-of-memory)

functions.name: sexp_transport_format
functions.signature: size_t sexp_transport_format(struct nettle_buffer *buffer, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Formats an s-expression using the transport encoding into buffer, according to the same format mini-language as sexp_format. Returns the number of output characters, or 0 on out-of-memory. If buffer == NULL, computes the required length only.
requirements: same argument and formatting requirements as sexp_format (buffer, format, and varargs must match the specifiers)
produces transport-encoded output; callers should ensure the consumer expects transport encoding
callers must check the return value: 0 indicates failure (out-of-memory)

functions.name: sexp_transport_vformat
functions.signature: size_t sexp_transport_vformat(struct nettle_buffer *buffer, const char *format, va_list args);
functions.description: va_list variant of sexp_transport_format. Formats using transport encoding with an existing va_list. Returns the number of output characters, or 0 on out-of-memory. If buffer == NULL, computes the required length only.
requirements: args must be an initialized va_list matching the format specifiers
same argument and formatting requirements as sexp_transport_format and sexp_format apply
callers must check the return value: 0 indicates failure (out-of-memory)

functions.name: nettle_sha1_init
functions.signature: void nettle_sha1_init(struct sha1_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA-1 hashing context. Call this before feeding data with update and finishing with digest. This is a name-mangled alias of sha1_init via the header’s macros.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer to a sha1_ctx structure.
ctx may be uninitialized memory; this function sets it to the initial SHA-1 state.
Must be called before nettle_sha1_update or nettle_sha1_digest on the same context.

functions.name: nettle_sha1_update
functions.signature: void nettle_sha1_update(struct sha1_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds input bytes into an initialized SHA-1 context. May be called zero or more times to process data in chunks. This is a name-mangled alias of sha1_update via the header’s macros.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer to a sha1_ctx previously initialized with nettle_sha1_init (or sha1_init).
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory; if length > 0, data must be non-null.
length is the number of bytes to process; any size_t value is allowed, including 0.

functions.name: nettle_sha1_digest
functions.signature: void nettle_sha1_digest(struct sha1_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-1 computation for the given context and writes the 20-byte digest to the provided buffer. Behavior regarding reusability of ctx after this call is not documented in this header. This is a name-mangled alias of sha1_digest via the header’s macros.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer to a sha1_ctx that has been initialized (and optionally updated) with nettle_sha1_init / nettle_sha1_update.
digest must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least SHA1_DIGEST_SIZE (20) bytes.
The effect on ctx after this call (e.g., whether it is reset or must be reinitialized) is unspecified in this header; callers should not assume reuse without reinitialization.

functions.name: nettle_sha1_compress
functions.signature: void nettle_sha1_compress(uint32_t *state, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Low-level SHA-1 compression over a single 64-byte block. Updates the 5-word state from one 512-bit block without handling padding or length encoding. DATA may be unaligned. Intended for advanced or internal use. This is a name-mangled alias of sha1_compress via the header’s macros.
requirements: state must point to exactly 5 uint32_t words holding the current SHA-1 state.
data must point to exactly 64 bytes (one SHA-1 block) of input; unaligned pointers are allowed.
No padding or length encoding is performed; caller must supply already chunked 64-byte message blocks and manage padding externally.
state and data must be non-null pointers.

functions.name: sha1_init
functions.signature: void sha1_init(struct sha1_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA-1 hashing context. Call before sha1_update and sha1_digest. The header also defines a macro mapping this to nettle_sha1_init.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer to a sha1_ctx structure.
ctx may be uninitialized memory; this function sets it to the initial SHA-1 state.
Must be called before sha1_update or sha1_digest on the same context.

functions.name: sha1_update
functions.signature: void sha1_update(struct sha1_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds input bytes into an initialized SHA-1 context. May be called zero or more times to process data in chunks.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer to a sha1_ctx previously initialized with sha1_init.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory; if length > 0, data must be non-null.
length is the number of bytes to process; any size_t value is allowed, including 0.

functions.name: sha1_digest
functions.signature: void sha1_digest(struct sha1_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-1 computation for the given context and writes the 20-byte digest to the provided buffer. Reusability of ctx after this call is not specified in this header.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer to a sha1_ctx that has been initialized (and optionally updated) with sha1_init / sha1_update.
digest must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least SHA1_DIGEST_SIZE (20) bytes.
The effect on ctx after this call (e.g., whether it is reset or must be reinitialized) is unspecified in this header; callers should not assume reuse without reinitialization.

functions.name: sha1_compress
functions.signature: void sha1_compress(uint32_t *state, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Low-level SHA-1 compression over a single 64-byte block. Updates the 5-word state from one 512-bit block without handling padding or length encoding. DATA may be unaligned. Intended for advanced or internal use.
requirements: state must point to exactly 5 uint32_t words holding the current SHA-1 state.
data must point to exactly 64 bytes (one SHA-1 block) of input; unaligned pointers are allowed.
No padding or length encoding is performed; caller must supply already chunked 64-byte message blocks and manage padding externally.
state and data must be non-null pointers.

functions.name: sha256_init
functions.signature: void sha256_init(struct sha256_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA-256 hashing context. Call this before feeding data via sha256_update and finishing with sha256_digest. Reinitializes the context for a new computation.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha256_ctx.
Must be called before any sha256_update or sha256_digest on the context.
After initialization, the context contains the SHA-256 initial state.

functions.name: sha256_update
functions.signature: void sha256_update(struct sha256_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds arbitrary-length data into an initialized SHA-256 context, updating the hash state. Can be called multiple times to process input in chunks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha256_ctx that has been initialized with sha256_init.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
It is permissible to call with length == 0; in that case data may be NULL (behavior not explicitly documented; typical convention).
May be called multiple times before calling sha256_digest.

functions.name: sha256_digest
functions.signature: void sha256_digest(struct sha256_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-256 computation and writes the 32-byte message digest to the provided buffer. Intended to be called after all input has been provided via sha256_update. Whether the context is reset or invalidated after digest is not specified in this header (unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha256_ctx that has been initialized (and optionally updated) for this computation.
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE (32) bytes.
Must be called after all intended sha256_update calls for the current computation.
Post-call state/reusability of ctx is unspecified in this header (unknown); callers should not assume it can be reused without reinitialization.

functions.name: sha256_compress
functions.signature: void sha256_compress(uint32_t *state, const uint8_t *input);
functions.description: Low-level SHA-256 compression function that processes one 64-byte message block, updating the 8-word internal state. Intended for internal/advanced use rather than typical application code.
requirements: state must point to an array of at least 8 uint32_t elements representing the current SHA-256 state.
input must point to at least SHA256_BLOCK_SIZE (64) bytes of readable memory containing one message block (including any required padding if used directly).
Caller is responsible for correct message padding and length processing when using this low-level routine.
Not safe to call with overlapping state and input buffers (typical constraint; overlap handling is unspecified).

functions.name: sha224_init
functions.signature: void sha224_init(struct sha256_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA-224 hashing context. SHA-224 is a truncated variant of SHA-256 with a different initial state. Use sha256_update (aliased as sha224_update) to feed data, and sha224_digest to finalize.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha256_ctx (SHA-224 shares the same context struct).
Must be called before any sha256_update/sha224_update or sha224_digest on the context.

functions.name: sha224_digest
functions.signature: void sha224_digest(struct sha256_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-224 computation and writes the 28-byte message digest. Use after feeding data via sha256_update/sha224_update. Post-finalization context behavior is unspecified (unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha256_ctx initialized via sha224_init.
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least SHA224_DIGEST_SIZE (28) bytes.
Must be called after all intended update calls for the current computation.
Post-call reusability/reset behavior is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: sha512_init
functions.signature: void sha512_init(struct sha512_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA-512 hashing context. Call before sha512_update and sha512_digest. Reinitializes the context for a new SHA-512 computation.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_ctx.
Must be called before any sha512_update or sha512_digest on the context.

functions.name: sha512_update
functions.signature: void sha512_update(struct sha512_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds arbitrary-length data into an initialized SHA-512 context, updating the hash state. Supports multiple calls for streaming input.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_ctx initialized with sha512_init (or a compatible variant init such as sha384_init/sha512_{224,256}_init when using those modes).
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
It is permissible to call with length == 0; in that case data may be NULL (behavior not explicitly documented; typical convention).
May be called multiple times before calling sha512_digest or the variant-specific digest.

functions.name: sha512_digest
functions.signature: void sha512_digest(struct sha512_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-512 computation and writes the 64-byte message digest. Intended to be called after all input has been provided via sha512_update. Post-finalization context behavior is not specified (unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_ctx that has been initialized (and optionally updated).
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least SHA512_DIGEST_SIZE (64) bytes.
Must be called after all intended sha512_update calls for the current computation.
Post-call reusability/reset behavior is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: sha512_compress
functions.signature: void sha512_compress(uint64_t *state, const uint8_t *input);
functions.description: Low-level SHA-512 compression function that processes one 128-byte message block, updating the 8-word 64-bit internal state. Intended for internal/advanced use.
requirements: state must point to an array of at least 8 uint64_t elements representing the current SHA-512 state.
input must point to at least SHA512_BLOCK_SIZE (128) bytes of readable memory containing one message block (including any required padding if used directly).
Caller must handle message padding and length processing when using this routine directly.
Not safe to call with overlapping state and input buffers (overlap handling unspecified).

functions.name: sha384_init
functions.signature: void sha384_init(struct sha512_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA-384 hashing context. SHA-384 is a truncated variant of SHA-512 with a different initial state. Use sha512_update (aliased as sha384_update) to feed data, and sha384_digest to finalize.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_ctx (SHA-384 shares the same context struct as SHA-512).
Must be called before any sha512_update/sha384_update or sha384_digest on the context.

functions.name: sha384_digest
functions.signature: void sha384_digest(struct sha512_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-384 computation and writes the 48-byte message digest. Use after feeding data via sha512_update/sha384_update. Post-finalization context behavior is unspecified (unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_ctx initialized via sha384_init.
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least SHA384_DIGEST_SIZE (48) bytes.
Must be called after all intended update calls for the current computation.
Post-call reusability/reset behavior is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: sha512_224_init
functions.signature: void sha512_224_init(struct sha512_224_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA-512/224 hashing context. This is a truncated variant of SHA-512 with a different initial state. Use sha512_update (aliased as sha512_224_update) to feed data, and sha512_224_digest to finalize. Note: sha512_224_ctx is a macro alias of sha512_ctx in this header.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_224_ctx (macro-alias of struct sha512_ctx).
Must be called before any sha512_update/sha512_224_update or sha512_224_digest on the context.

functions.name: sha512_224_digest
functions.signature: void sha512_224_digest(struct sha512_224_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-512/224 computation and writes the 28-byte message digest. Use after feeding data via sha512_update/sha512_224_update. Post-finalization context behavior is unspecified (unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_224_ctx (alias of sha512_ctx) initialized via sha512_224_init.
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least SHA512_224_DIGEST_SIZE (28) bytes.
Must be called after all intended update calls for the current computation.
Post-call reusability/reset behavior is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: sha512_256_init
functions.signature: void sha512_256_init(struct sha512_256_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA-512/256 hashing context. This is a truncated variant of SHA-512 with a different initial state. Use sha512_update (aliased as sha512_256_update) to feed data, and sha512_256_digest to finalize. Note: sha512_256_ctx is a macro alias of sha512_ctx in this header.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_256_ctx (macro-alias of struct sha512_ctx).
Must be called before any sha512_update/sha512_256_update or sha512_256_digest on the context.

functions.name: sha512_256_digest
functions.signature: void sha512_256_digest(struct sha512_256_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-512/256 computation and writes the 32-byte message digest. Use after feeding data via sha512_update/sha512_256_update. Post-finalization context behavior is unspecified (unknown).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct sha512_256_ctx (alias of sha512_ctx) initialized via sha512_256_init.
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least SHA512_256_DIGEST_SIZE (32) bytes.
Must be called after all intended update calls for the current computation.
Post-call reusability/reset behavior is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: sha3_permute
functions.signature: void sha3_permute(struct sha3_state *state);
functions.description: Applies the Keccak-f[1600] permutation to the provided SHA3 state (5x5 matrix of 64‑bit words). Intended for low-level use inside SHA3/Keccak processing.
requirements: state must be non-NULL and point to a valid, initialized struct sha3_state whose a[25] is writable.
Caller must expect state to be modified in place.
No threading/aliasing guarantees are specified; do not concurrently mutate the same state from multiple threads.

functions.name: sha3_init
functions.signature: void sha3_init(struct sha3_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a SHA3 context for subsequent SHA3 hashing or SHAKE operations. Sets internal state, index, and shake flag to a clean starting state.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and point to writable memory.
Must be called before any corresponding sha3_*_update, sha3_*_digest, or sha3_*_shake/sha3_*_shake_output calls on this context.
The same ctx must not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: sha3_128_update
functions.signature: void sha3_128_update(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Absorbs input bytes into the SHA3-128 context. May be called to provide message data prior to finalization or SHAKE output.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized with sha3_init.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
Behavior for length == 0 is not specified in this header (assumed safe but not stated).
Do not pass NULL for data when length > 0.

functions.name: sha3_128_shake
functions.signature: void sha3_128_shake(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Produces length bytes of SHAKE128 output from the context into digest (XOF). Intended as an alternative to fixed-size digests with arbitrary output length.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized; typically called after feeding input via sha3_128_update.
digest must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
length specifies the exact number of output bytes to write.
Whether this function may be called multiple times to extend output is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: sha3_128_shake_output
functions.signature: void sha3_128_shake_output(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Writes length bytes of SHAKE128 output to digest from an initialized/absorbed context. Intended for output retrieval after initializing SHAKE output state.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized; typically called after feeding input via sha3_128_update.
digest must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
length specifies the exact number of output bytes to write.
Whether this function can be called multiple times to incrementally retrieve output is not stated in this header (unknown).

functions.name: sha3_224_update
functions.signature: void sha3_224_update(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Absorbs input bytes into the SHA3-224 context prior to finalization.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized with sha3_init.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
Behavior for length == 0 is not specified in this header (assumed safe but not stated).
Do not pass NULL for data when length > 0.

functions.name: sha3_224_digest
functions.signature: void sha3_224_digest(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA3-224 computation and writes the 28-byte digest to the provided buffer.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized; typically called after zero or more sha3_224_update calls.
digest must point to at least SHA3_224_DIGEST_SIZE (28) bytes of writable memory.
After finalization, further updates are not described here (unknown semantics).

functions.name: sha3_256_update
functions.signature: void sha3_256_update(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Absorbs input bytes into the SHA3-256 context prior to finalization or SHAKE-256 output.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized with sha3_init.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
Behavior for length == 0 is not specified in this header (assumed safe but not stated).
Do not pass NULL for data when length > 0.

functions.name: sha3_256_digest
functions.signature: void sha3_256_digest(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA3-256 computation and writes the 32-byte digest to the provided buffer.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized; typically called after zero or more sha3_256_update calls.
digest must point to at least SHA3_256_DIGEST_SIZE (32) bytes of writable memory.
After finalization, further updates are not described here (unknown semantics).

functions.name: sha3_256_shake
functions.signature: void sha3_256_shake(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Produces length bytes of SHAKE256 output from the context into digest (XOF). Alternative to fixed-size SHA3-256 digest, with arbitrary output size.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized; typically called after zero or more sha3_256_update calls.
digest must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
length specifies the exact number of output bytes to write.
Per the header comment, unlike sha3_256_shake_output this single-shot function is not intended for multiple incremental output calls; repeated calls for additional output are not supported.

functions.name: sha3_256_shake_output
functions.signature: void sha3_256_shake_output(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Retrieves SHAKE256 output incrementally. Can be called multiple times to produce additional XOF bytes after initializing the output phase.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized; typically called after zero or more sha3_256_update calls and after the SHAKE output phase is initialized internally.
digest must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
length specifies the exact number of output bytes to write.
This function may be called multiple times to append more output, as explicitly documented in the header.

functions.name: sha3_384_update
functions.signature: void sha3_384_update(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Absorbs input bytes into the SHA3-384 context prior to finalization.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized with sha3_init.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
Behavior for length == 0 is not specified in this header (assumed safe but not stated).
Do not pass NULL for data when length > 0.

functions.name: sha3_384_digest
functions.signature: void sha3_384_digest(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA3-384 computation and writes the 48-byte digest to the provided buffer.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized; typically called after zero or more sha3_384_update calls.
digest must point to at least SHA3_384_DIGEST_SIZE (48) bytes of writable memory.
After finalization, further updates are not described here (unknown semantics).

functions.name: sha3_512_update
functions.signature: void sha3_512_update(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Absorbs input bytes into the SHA3-512 context prior to finalization.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized with sha3_init.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
Behavior for length == 0 is not specified in this header (assumed safe but not stated).
Do not pass NULL for data when length > 0.

functions.name: sha3_512_digest
functions.signature: void sha3_512_digest(struct sha3_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA3-512 computation and writes the 64-byte digest to the provided buffer.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and previously initialized; typically called after zero or more sha3_512_update calls.
digest must point to at least SHA3_512_DIGEST_SIZE (64) bytes of writable memory.
After finalization, further updates are not described here (unknown semantics).

functions.name: sha3_128_init
functions.signature: void sha3_128_init(struct sha3_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Alias macro for sha3_init; initializes a SHA3 context for use with SHA3-128 routines. Provided for compatibility with older Nettle versions.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and writable.
Must be called before any sha3_128_update/sha3_128_shake/sha3_128_shake_output calls on this context.

functions.name: sha3_224_init
functions.signature: void sha3_224_init(struct sha3_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Alias macro for sha3_init; initializes a SHA3 context for use with SHA3-224 routines. Provided for compatibility with older Nettle versions.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and writable.
Must be called before any sha3_224_update/sha3_224_digest calls on this context.

functions.name: sha3_256_init
functions.signature: void sha3_256_init(struct sha3_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Alias macro for sha3_init; initializes a SHA3 context for use with SHA3-256/SHAKE256 routines. Provided for compatibility with older Nettle versions.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and writable.
Must be called before any sha3_256_update/sha3_256_digest/sha3_256_shake/sha3_256_shake_output calls on this context.

functions.name: sha3_384_init
functions.signature: void sha3_384_init(struct sha3_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Alias macro for sha3_init; initializes a SHA3 context for use with SHA3-384 routines. Provided for compatibility with older Nettle versions.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and writable.
Must be called before any sha3_384_update/sha3_384_digest calls on this context.

functions.name: sha3_512_init
functions.signature: void sha3_512_init(struct sha3_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Alias macro for sha3_init; initializes a SHA3 context for use with SHA3-512 routines. Provided for compatibility with older Nettle versions.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and writable.
Must be called before any sha3_512_update/sha3_512_digest calls on this context.

functions.name: sm3_init
functions.signature: void sm3_init(struct sm3_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes an SM3 hashing context. Call this before supplying any input data via sm3_update and before obtaining the final 32-byte digest via sm3_digest. Sets up ctx with the SM3 initial state and clears its internal buffers.
requirements: ctx must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable struct sm3_ctx.
Must be called before any sm3_update or sm3_digest on the same context.
The same context may be reused by calling sm3_init again to start a new computation.

functions.name: sm3_update
functions.signature: void sm3_update(struct sm3_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds input bytes into an initialized SM3 context for hashing. Can be invoked repeatedly to process data in chunks; the total hashed message is the concatenation of all provided chunks.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and must have been initialized with sm3_init.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
length is the number of bytes to hash; it may be zero (no effect).
May be called multiple times between sm3_init and sm3_digest.

functions.name: sm3_digest
functions.signature: void sm3_digest(struct sm3_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the SM3 computation and writes the 32-byte message digest to the caller-provided buffer. Expected usage: call after sm3_init and any number of sm3_update calls. The digest size is fixed at SM3_DIGEST_SIZE (32 bytes). Whether the context is reset or invalidated after this call is not specified in this header (unknown).
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and should have been initialized with sm3_init (optionally followed by one or more sm3_update calls).
digest must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least SM3_DIGEST_SIZE (32) bytes.
The state of ctx after this call (e.g., whether it can be updated further or requires reinitialization) is not specified here and should be treated as unknown.

functions.name: sm4_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: void sm4_set_encrypt_key(struct sm4_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes an SM4 key schedule in ctx for encryption using the 128-bit key at key. Call this before sm4_crypt to perform encryption with this context. The function writes round keys into ctx and performs no I/O or allocation. Returns no status; invalid inputs lead to undefined behavior.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an sm4_ctx structure.
key must point to at least SM4_KEY_SIZE (16) bytes of key material.
Must be called before sm4_crypt when using this ctx for encryption.
Do not call concurrently on the same ctx from multiple threads (ctx is mutated).
Function returns void; callers must not expect error reporting.

functions.name: sm4_set_decrypt_key
functions.signature: void sm4_set_decrypt_key(struct sm4_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes an SM4 key schedule in ctx for decryption using the 128-bit key at key. Use this prior to sm4_crypt to perform decryption with this context. The function prepares round keys for decryption and does not allocate or return a status.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an sm4_ctx structure.
key must point to at least SM4_KEY_SIZE (16) bytes of key material.
Must be called before sm4_crypt when using this ctx for decryption.
Do not call concurrently on the same ctx from multiple threads (ctx is mutated).
Function returns void; callers must not expect error reporting.

functions.name: sm4_crypt
functions.signature: void sm4_crypt(const struct sm4_ctx *context, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts length bytes of data from src to dst using the SM4 key schedule in context. The operation performed (encryption or decryption) depends on whether context was initialized with sm4_set_encrypt_key or sm4_set_decrypt_key. This is a raw block operation (ECB-style) over full blocks; it does not implement a mode, padding, or IV handling.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to an sm4_ctx previously initialized via sm4_set_encrypt_key (for encryption) or sm4_set_decrypt_key (for decryption).
length must be a multiple of SM4_BLOCK_SIZE (16); partial blocks are not supported.
dst must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.
src must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes.
If in-place operation (dst == src) is desired: in Nettle block ciphers this is typically supported, but it is not stated here; if unsure, avoid overlapping buffers.
Function returns void; callers must not expect error reporting.
The function performs no padding or mode of operation; callers must implement any desired mode (e.g., CBC, CTR) and block chaining externally.

functions.name: streebog512_init
functions.signature: void streebog512_init(struct streebog512_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a Streebog-512 hashing context. Call this before any update or digest to set the internal state, counters, and buffer to their initial values. Intended for computing GOST R 34.11-2012 (Streebog) 512-bit hashes.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a streebog512_ctx structure.
Must be called before streebog512_update or streebog512_digest on the same context.
The same context must not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: streebog512_update
functions.signature: void streebog512_update(struct streebog512_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds message bytes into an initialized Streebog-512 hashing context. May be called multiple times to process a message in chunks. The function absorbs exactly 'length' bytes from 'data' into the running hash state.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a streebog512_ctx structure initialized by streebog512_init.
data must point to at least 'length' bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
length may be zero; behavior for data == NULL when length == 0 is unknown (not specified).
Do not call after finalization if the implementation treats streebog512_digest as final; whether the context remains usable after digest is unknown.
The same context must not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: streebog512_digest
functions.signature: void streebog512_digest(struct streebog512_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the Streebog-512 hashing operation and writes the 64-byte message digest to 'digest'. Use after all data has been provided via streebog512_update.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a streebog512_ctx structure that has been initialized (and optionally updated).
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least STREEBOG512_DIGEST_SIZE (64) bytes.
Must be called after streebog512_init and after all desired streebog512_update calls.
Whether ctx is reset or remains valid for reuse after this call is unknown (not specified); if reuse is desired, reinitialize with streebog512_init to be safe.
The same context must not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: streebog256_init
functions.signature: void streebog256_init(struct streebog256_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes a Streebog-256 hashing context. streebog256_ctx is an alias of streebog512_ctx; this sets up the internal state for computing the 256-bit variant of GOST R 34.11-2012.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a streebog256_ctx (alias of streebog512_ctx).
Must be called before streebog256_update or streebog256_digest on the same context.
The same context must not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: streebog256_update
functions.signature: void streebog256_update(struct streebog256_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds message bytes into an initialized Streebog-256 hashing context. This is a macro alias to the Streebog-512 update implementation, but accepts a streebog256_ctx (alias of streebog512_ctx). May be called multiple times to process input in chunks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a streebog256_ctx (alias of streebog512_ctx) initialized by streebog256_init.
data must point to at least 'length' bytes of readable memory when length > 0.
length may be zero; behavior for data == NULL when length == 0 is unknown (not specified).
Do not call after finalization if the implementation treats streebog256_digest as final; whether the context remains usable after digest is unknown.
The same context must not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: streebog256_digest
functions.signature: void streebog256_digest(struct streebog256_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the Streebog-256 hashing operation and writes the 32-byte message digest to 'digest'. Use after all data has been provided via streebog256_update.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a streebog256_ctx structure that has been initialized (and optionally updated).
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least STREEBOG256_DIGEST_SIZE (32) bytes.
Must be called after streebog256_init and after all desired streebog256_update calls.
Whether ctx is reset or remains valid for reuse after this call is unknown (not specified); if reuse is desired, reinitialize with streebog256_init to be safe.
The same context must not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: twofish_set_key
functions.signature: void twofish_set_key(struct twofish_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Twofish cipher context with a user-supplied key of variable length. Accepts 128-, 192-, or 256-bit keys (16, 24, or 32 bytes). Use this when the key size is not known at compile time. After successful initialization, the context can be used with twofish_encrypt and twofish_decrypt. No return value; caller must ensure inputs are valid.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to struct twofish_ctx.
length must be exactly 16, 24, or 32 bytes; other lengths are invalid per header comments.
key must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
Call this function before any call to twofish_encrypt or twofish_decrypt that uses ctx.
This function performs no padding; it only sets up the key schedule.
Error handling: function returns void; caller must validate inputs to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: twofish128_set_key
functions.signature: void twofish128_set_key(struct twofish_ctx *context, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Twofish cipher context with a 128-bit (16-byte) key. Convenience variant of twofish_set_key for fixed-size keys. After initialization, use twofish_encrypt/twofish_decrypt with this context.
requirements: context must be a valid, writable pointer to struct twofish_ctx.
key must point to at least 16 bytes (TWOFISH128_KEY_SIZE) of readable memory.
Call this function before any call to twofish_encrypt or twofish_decrypt that uses context.
No padding or error code is provided; function returns void.

functions.name: twofish192_set_key
functions.signature: void twofish192_set_key(struct twofish_ctx *context, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Twofish cipher context with a 192-bit (24-byte) key. Convenience variant for fixed-size keys. Use the resulting context with twofish_encrypt/twofish_decrypt.
requirements: context must be a valid, writable pointer to struct twofish_ctx.
key must point to at least 24 bytes (TWOFISH192_KEY_SIZE) of readable memory.
Call this function before any call to twofish_encrypt or twofish_decrypt that uses context.
No padding or error code is provided; function returns void.

functions.name: twofish256_set_key
functions.signature: void twofish256_set_key(struct twofish_ctx *context, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a Twofish cipher context with a 256-bit (32-byte) key. Convenience variant for fixed-size keys. Use the initialized context with twofish_encrypt/twofish_decrypt.
requirements: context must be a valid, writable pointer to struct twofish_ctx.
key must point to at least 32 bytes (TWOFISH256_KEY_SIZE) of readable memory.
Call this function before any call to twofish_encrypt or twofish_decrypt that uses context.
No padding or error code is provided; function returns void.

functions.name: twofish_encrypt
functions.signature: void twofish_encrypt(const struct twofish_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Encrypts data using Twofish in block mode with the provided context. Processes whole blocks of 16 bytes (TWOFISH_BLOCK_SIZE); no padding is performed. Intended for callers that manage block alignment and mode of operation externally (e.g., ECB, CBC, CTR wrappers).
requirements: ctx must point to an initialized twofish_ctx (initialized via one of the twofish*_set_key functions).
length must be a multiple of 16 (TWOFISH_BLOCK_SIZE); no partial blocks are handled.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory, and dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst is not specified in this header; to be safe, use non-overlapping buffers or exactly the same pointer for in-place operation only if confirmed elsewhere.
Function returns void; caller must enforce the above preconditions and manage any mode-specific IVs or padding externally.

functions.name: twofish_decrypt
functions.signature: void twofish_decrypt(const struct twofish_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src);
functions.description: Decrypts data using Twofish in block mode with the provided context. Processes whole 16-byte blocks; no padding is handled. Intended to be used by higher-level mode implementations (e.g., CBC, CTR) that ensure block alignment.
requirements: ctx must point to an initialized twofish_ctx (initialized via one of the twofish*_set_key functions).
length must be a multiple of 16 (TWOFISH_BLOCK_SIZE); no partial blocks are handled.
If length > 0, src must point to at least length bytes of readable memory, and dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst is not specified in this header; to be safe, use non-overlapping buffers or exactly the same pointer for in-place operation only if confirmed elsewhere.
Function returns void; caller must enforce the above preconditions and manage any mode-specific IVs or padding externally.

functions.name: umac32_set_key
functions.signature: void umac32_set_key(struct umac32_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a UMAC-32 context with a 128-bit key. Sets up subkeys and resets the internal nonce to zero. Use before processing any message data with umac32_update and before producing tags with umac32_digest. You may override the nonce later with umac32_set_nonce if desired.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an initialized struct umac32_ctx.
key must point to exactly UMAC_KEY_SIZE (AES128_KEY_SIZE) bytes.
Must be called before umac32_update, umac32_set_nonce, or umac32_digest on the same context.
Sets the internal nonce to zero (subsequent messages will start from nonce 0 unless overridden).

functions.name: umac64_set_key
functions.signature: void umac64_set_key(struct umac64_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a UMAC-64 context with a 128-bit key. Sets up subkeys and resets the internal nonce to zero. Call before update/digest operations; nonce can optionally be set with umac64_set_nonce.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an initialized struct umac64_ctx.
key must point to exactly UMAC_KEY_SIZE (AES128_KEY_SIZE) bytes.
Must be called before umac64_update, umac64_set_nonce, or umac64_digest on the same context.
Sets the internal nonce to zero.

functions.name: umac96_set_key
functions.signature: void umac96_set_key(struct umac96_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a UMAC-96 context with a 128-bit key and resets the internal nonce to zero. Call before processing data or computing tags. Nonce can be overridden via umac96_set_nonce.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an initialized struct umac96_ctx.
key must point to exactly UMAC_KEY_SIZE (AES128_KEY_SIZE) bytes.
Must be called before umac96_update, umac96_set_nonce, or umac96_digest on the same context.
Sets the internal nonce to zero.

functions.name: umac128_set_key
functions.signature: void umac128_set_key(struct umac128_ctx *ctx, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes a UMAC-128 context with a 128-bit key and resets the internal nonce to zero. Use prior to update/digest; nonce may be supplied explicitly via umac128_set_nonce.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an initialized struct umac128_ctx.
key must point to exactly UMAC_KEY_SIZE (AES128_KEY_SIZE) bytes.
Must be called before umac128_update, umac128_set_nonce, or umac128_digest on the same context.
Sets the internal nonce to zero.

functions.name: umac32_set_nonce
functions.signature: void umac32_set_nonce(struct umac32_ctx *ctx, size_t nonce_length, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Sets the per-message nonce for UMAC-32. If not used, messages get incrementing nonces starting from zero. Use this to supply an explicit nonce value before processing a message.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac32_set_key.
nonce_length must be between UMAC_MIN_NONCE_SIZE and UMAC_MAX_NONCE_SIZE (inclusive).
nonce must point to at least nonce_length bytes.
Call before umac32_update/umac32_digest for the message to which this nonce applies.

functions.name: umac64_set_nonce
functions.signature: void umac64_set_nonce(struct umac64_ctx *ctx, size_t nonce_length, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Sets the per-message nonce for UMAC-64. Optional; if omitted, nonces increment starting from zero across messages. Supply before processing a message to control the nonce.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac64_set_key.
nonce_length must be between UMAC_MIN_NONCE_SIZE and UMAC_MAX_NONCE_SIZE (inclusive).
nonce must point to at least nonce_length bytes.
Call before umac64_update/umac64_digest for the message to which this nonce applies.

functions.name: umac96_set_nonce
functions.signature: void umac96_set_nonce(struct umac96_ctx *ctx, size_t nonce_length, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Sets the per-message nonce for UMAC-96. Optional; without it, nonces auto-increment from zero per message. Use to specify an explicit nonce for the next tag.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac96_set_key.
nonce_length must be between UMAC_MIN_NONCE_SIZE and UMAC_MAX_NONCE_SIZE (inclusive).
nonce must point to at least nonce_length bytes.
Call before umac96_update/umac96_digest for the message to which this nonce applies.

functions.name: umac128_set_nonce
functions.signature: void umac128_set_nonce(struct umac128_ctx *ctx, size_t nonce_length, const uint8_t *nonce);
functions.description: Sets the per-message nonce for UMAC-128. Optional; otherwise nonces increment starting from zero. Call before processing a message if you need a specific nonce.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac128_set_key.
nonce_length must be between UMAC_MIN_NONCE_SIZE and UMAC_MAX_NONCE_SIZE (inclusive).
nonce must point to at least nonce_length bytes.
Call before umac128_update/umac128_digest for the message to which this nonce applies.

functions.name: umac32_update
functions.signature: void umac32_update(struct umac32_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds message data into the UMAC-32 computation. Can be called multiple times to process a message in chunks before finalizing with umac32_digest.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac32_set_key.
If a specific nonce is required, call umac32_set_nonce before the first update for that message.
data must point to at least length bytes; if length is 0, data may be NULL.
May be called zero or more times before umac32_digest for a message.

functions.name: umac64_update
functions.signature: void umac64_update(struct umac64_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds message data into the UMAC-64 computation. Supports incremental processing; call repeatedly before umac64_digest.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac64_set_key.
If a specific nonce is required, call umac64_set_nonce before the first update for that message.
data must point to at least length bytes; if length is 0, data may be NULL.
May be called zero or more times before umac64_digest for a message.

functions.name: umac96_update
functions.signature: void umac96_update(struct umac96_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds message data into the UMAC-96 computation. Use for streaming input; finalize with umac96_digest.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac96_set_key.
If a specific nonce is required, call umac96_set_nonce before the first update for that message.
data must point to at least length bytes; if length is 0, data may be NULL.
May be called zero or more times before umac96_digest for a message.

functions.name: umac128_update
functions.signature: void umac128_update(struct umac128_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds message data into the UMAC-128 computation. Can be called repeatedly to process a message; finalize with umac128_digest.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac128_set_key.
If a specific nonce is required, call umac128_set_nonce before the first update for that message.
data must point to at least length bytes; if length is 0, data may be NULL.
May be called zero or more times before umac128_digest for a message.

functions.name: umac32_digest
functions.signature: void umac32_digest(struct umac32_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the current UMAC-32 computation and writes a 4-byte tag to digest. After producing the tag, the function increments the internal nonce for the next message. Typically called after zero or more umac32_update calls.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac32_set_key.
digest must point to at least UMAC32_DIGEST_SIZE (4) writable bytes.
Produces a tag for the current message state; after return, the internal nonce is incremented for subsequent messages.

functions.name: umac64_digest
functions.signature: void umac64_digest(struct umac64_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the current UMAC-64 computation and writes an 8-byte tag to digest. The function increments the internal nonce afterwards. Call after zero or more umac64_update calls.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac64_set_key.
digest must point to at least UMAC64_DIGEST_SIZE (8) writable bytes.
After return, the internal nonce is incremented for subsequent messages.

functions.name: umac96_digest
functions.signature: void umac96_digest(struct umac96_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the current UMAC-96 computation and writes a 12-byte tag to digest. The function increments the internal nonce afterwards. Call after zero or more umac96_update calls.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac96_set_key.
digest must point to at least UMAC96_DIGEST_SIZE (12) writable bytes.
After return, the internal nonce is incremented for subsequent messages.

functions.name: umac128_digest
functions.signature: void umac128_digest(struct umac128_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *digest);
functions.description: Finalizes the current UMAC-128 computation and writes a 16-byte tag to digest. The function increments the internal nonce afterwards. Call after zero or more umac128_update calls.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with umac128_set_key.
digest must point to at least UMAC128_DIGEST_SIZE (16) writable bytes.
After return, the internal nonce is incremented for subsequent messages.

functions.name: xts_encrypt_message
functions.signature: void xts_encrypt_message(const void *enc_ctx, const void *twk_ctx, nettle_cipher_func *encf, const uint8_t *tweak, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src)
functions.description: Encrypts a message using XTS (XEX-based tweaked-codebook mode with ciphertext stealing). Uses the caller-provided block-cipher encryption function encf and associated contexts: enc_ctx for data encryption and twk_ctx for tweak computation. The 16-byte tweak seeds the per-block tweak. Supports ciphertext stealing for inputs not an exact multiple of the block size.
requirements: enc_ctx must point to a valid, initialized encryption context compatible with encf and 16-byte block ciphers (e.g., AES).
twk_ctx must point to a valid, initialized encryption context for the same cipher, used for tweak processing.
encf must be a block-cipher encryption function matching the type nettle_cipher_func and the provided contexts; block size must be XTS_BLOCK_SIZE (16 bytes).
tweak must point to at least 16 bytes (XTS_BLOCK_SIZE).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable data.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory; in-place operation is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.
length should be >= 16 bytes; XTS with ciphertext stealing supports any length >= one block (exact minimum not explicitly stated in the header).
The cipher contexts and encf must correspond to the same algorithm and keying; mismatched contexts/functions are invalid.
Behavior for length == 0 is unspecified; callers should avoid calling with zero length.

functions.name: xts_decrypt_message
functions.signature: void xts_decrypt_message(const void *dec_ctx, const void *twk_ctx, nettle_cipher_func *decf, nettle_cipher_func *encf, const uint8_t *tweak, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src)
functions.description: Decrypts a message using XTS mode. Requires both the block-cipher decryption function decf (with dec_ctx) for data blocks and the encryption function encf (with twk_ctx) for tweak computation. The 16-byte tweak is the same value used during encryption. Supports ciphertext stealing for non-multiple block lengths.
requirements: dec_ctx must point to a valid, initialized decryption context compatible with decf and 16-byte block ciphers (e.g., AES).
twk_ctx must point to a valid, initialized encryption context for the same cipher, used for tweak processing.
decf must be a block-cipher decryption function matching nettle_cipher_func and compatible with dec_ctx; block size must be 16 bytes.
encf must be a block-cipher encryption function matching nettle_cipher_func and compatible with twk_ctx; block size must be 16 bytes.
tweak must point to at least 16 bytes (XTS_BLOCK_SIZE) and match the tweak used during encryption.
src must point to at least length bytes of readable data.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory; in-place operation is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.
length should be >= 16 bytes; ciphertext stealing allows any length >= one block (exact minimum not explicitly stated in the header).
The cipher contexts and functions must correspond to the same algorithm and keying used for encryption; mismatches are invalid.
Behavior for length == 0 is unspecified; callers should avoid calling with zero length.

functions.name: xts_aes128_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: void xts_aes128_set_encrypt_key(struct xts_aes128_key *xts_key, const uint8_t *key)
functions.description: Initializes an XTS key for AES-128 encryption. Populates both the data cipher and tweak cipher subkeys in xts_key using the provided raw key material (commonly two concatenated 128-bit keys).
requirements: xts_key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to storage for the key; its fields will be initialized.
key must point to sufficient key material for two AES-128 keys (commonly 32 bytes); the exact required size is not stated in this header but is standard for XTS-AES-128.
Must be called before xts_aes128_encrypt_message and typically before decryption if using separate set_decrypt_key.
The same key bytes must be used consistently for encryption and decryption for correct operation.

functions.name: xts_aes128_set_decrypt_key
functions.signature: void xts_aes128_set_decrypt_key(struct xts_aes128_key *xts_key, const uint8_t *key)
functions.description: Initializes an XTS key for AES-128 decryption. Sets up the data decryption key schedule and the tweak cipher using the provided raw key material (commonly two concatenated 128-bit keys).
requirements: xts_key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to storage for the key; its fields will be initialized.
key must point to sufficient key material for two AES-128 keys (commonly 32 bytes); the exact required size is not stated in this header but is standard for XTS-AES-128.
Must be called before xts_aes128_decrypt_message.
If encryption will also be performed, the corresponding encrypt key setup must be done via xts_aes128_set_encrypt_key.

functions.name: xts_aes128_encrypt_message
functions.signature: void xts_aes128_encrypt_message(const struct xts_aes128_key *xtskey, const uint8_t *tweak, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src)
functions.description: Encrypts a message with AES-128 in XTS mode using a pre-initialized xts_aes128_key. The 16-byte tweak seeds the per-block tweak. Supports ciphertext stealing for non-multiple block lengths.
requirements: xtskey must point to a key structure initialized by xts_aes128_set_encrypt_key.
tweak must point to at least 16 bytes (XTS_BLOCK_SIZE).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable data.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory; in-place operation is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.
length should be >= 16 bytes; ciphertext stealing allows any length >= one block (exact minimum not explicitly stated in the header).
Behavior for length == 0 is unspecified; callers should avoid calling with zero length.

functions.name: xts_aes128_decrypt_message
functions.signature: void xts_aes128_decrypt_message(const struct xts_aes128_key *xts_key, const uint8_t *tweak, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src)
functions.description: Decrypts a message with AES-128 in XTS mode using a pre-initialized xts_aes128_key. The 16-byte tweak must match the value used during encryption. Supports ciphertext stealing for non-multiple block lengths.
requirements: xts_key must point to a key structure initialized by xts_aes128_set_decrypt_key.
tweak must point to at least 16 bytes (XTS_BLOCK_SIZE) and match the encryption tweak.
src must point to at least length bytes of readable data.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory; in-place operation is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.
length should be >= 16 bytes; ciphertext stealing allows any length >= one block (exact minimum not explicitly stated in the header).
Behavior for length == 0 is unspecified; callers should avoid calling with zero length.

functions.name: xts_aes256_set_encrypt_key
functions.signature: void xts_aes256_set_encrypt_key(struct xts_aes256_key *xts_key, const uint8_t *key)
functions.description: Initializes an XTS key for AES-256 encryption. Populates both the data cipher and tweak cipher subkeys in xts_key using the provided raw key material (commonly two concatenated 256-bit keys).
requirements: xts_key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to storage for the key; its fields will be initialized.
key must point to sufficient key material for two AES-256 keys (commonly 64 bytes); the exact required size is not stated in this header but is standard for XTS-AES-256.
Must be called before xts_aes256_encrypt_message and typically before decryption if using separate set_decrypt_key.
The same key bytes must be used consistently for encryption and decryption for correct operation.

functions.name: xts_aes256_set_decrypt_key
functions.signature: void xts_aes256_set_decrypt_key(struct xts_aes256_key *xts_key, const uint8_t *key)
functions.description: Initializes an XTS key for AES-256 decryption. Sets up the data decryption key schedule and the tweak cipher using the provided raw key material (commonly two concatenated 256-bit keys).
requirements: xts_key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to storage for the key; its fields will be initialized.
key must point to sufficient key material for two AES-256 keys (commonly 64 bytes); the exact required size is not stated in this header but is standard for XTS-AES-256.
Must be called before xts_aes256_decrypt_message.
If encryption will also be performed, the corresponding encrypt key setup must be done via xts_aes256_set_encrypt_key.

functions.name: xts_aes256_encrypt_message
functions.signature: void xts_aes256_encrypt_message(const struct xts_aes256_key *xts_key, const uint8_t *tweak, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src)
functions.description: Encrypts a message with AES-256 in XTS mode using a pre-initialized xts_aes256_key. The 16-byte tweak seeds the per-block tweak. Supports ciphertext stealing for non-multiple block lengths.
requirements: xts_key must point to a key structure initialized by xts_aes256_set_encrypt_key.
tweak must point to at least 16 bytes (XTS_BLOCK_SIZE).
src must point to at least length bytes of readable data.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory; in-place operation is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.
length should be >= 16 bytes; ciphertext stealing allows any length >= one block (exact minimum not explicitly stated in the header).
Behavior for length == 0 is unspecified; callers should avoid calling with zero length.

functions.name: xts_aes256_decrypt_message
functions.signature: void xts_aes256_decrypt_message(const struct xts_aes256_key *xts_key, const uint8_t *tweak, size_t length, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src)
functions.description: Decrypts a message with AES-256 in XTS mode using a pre-initialized xts_aes256_key. The 16-byte tweak must match the value used during encryption. Supports ciphertext stealing for non-multiple block lengths.
requirements: xts_key must point to a key structure initialized by xts_aes256_set_decrypt_key.
tweak must point to at least 16 bytes (XTS_BLOCK_SIZE) and match the encryption tweak.
src must point to at least length bytes of readable data.
dst must point to at least length bytes of writable memory; in-place operation is unknown; if unsure, use non-overlapping buffers.
length should be >= 16 bytes; ciphertext stealing allows any length >= one block (exact minimum not explicitly stated in the header).
Behavior for length == 0 is unspecified; callers should avoid calling with zero length.

functions.name: yarrow256_init
functions.signature: void yarrow256_init(struct yarrow256_ctx *ctx, unsigned nsources, struct yarrow_source *sources);
functions.description: Initializes a Yarrow-256 PRNG context with the specified number of entropy sources. Sets up internal hash pools, key/counter state, and associates the provided sources array with the context. Use this before any seeding, updating, or generating random bytes.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a yarrow256_ctx.
sources must point to an array of at least nsources elements when nsources > 0; may be NULL only if nsources == 0.
Must be called before yarrow256_seed, yarrow256_update, yarrow256_random, or reseed functions.
nsources must fit in an unsigned and match the number of available source descriptors provided by the caller.

functions.name: yarrow256_seed
functions.signature: void yarrow256_seed(struct yarrow256_ctx *ctx, size_t length, const uint8_t *seed_file);
functions.description: Seeds the Yarrow-256 context from a seed file buffer. Intended to quickly bring the PRNG to a seeded state using externally stored entropy (e.g., from previous runs).
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via yarrow256_init.
seed_file must point to a buffer of at least length bytes.
length should be equal to YARROW256_SEED_FILE_SIZE (2 * AES_BLOCK_SIZE) for a complete seed file; other lengths are not documented and may be invalid.
Caller must ensure the seed_file contains high-quality entropy.
Must not be called with a NULL ctx or NULL seed_file when length > 0.

functions.name: yarrow256_update
functions.signature: int yarrow256_update(struct yarrow256_ctx *ctx, unsigned source, unsigned entropy, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Feeds new entropy samples into the Yarrow-256 pools from a specific source and may trigger a reseed. Returns 1 if a reseed occurred as a result of this update, otherwise 0.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via yarrow256_init.
source must be a valid source index: 0 <= source < ctx->nsources.
data must point to a buffer of at least length bytes; may be NULL only if length == 0.
entropy is an estimate (in bits) of the entropy contributed by data; must be a non-negative value that does not exceed the total number of bits in data (8 * length).
May be called multiple times; caller should handle the return value: 1 indicates a reseed was performed.

functions.name: yarrow256_random
functions.signature: void yarrow256_random(struct yarrow256_ctx *ctx, size_t length, uint8_t *dst);
functions.description: Generates cryptographically strong pseudorandom bytes and writes them to dst. Uses AES-256 in counter mode with internal key/counter derived via Yarrow reseeding.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via yarrow256_init.
ctx should be in a seeded state before calling (check with yarrow256_is_seeded or seed/update appropriately); generating before seeding may yield predictable output.
dst must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.
length may be zero; in that case, dst is not dereferenced.

functions.name: yarrow256_is_seeded
functions.signature: int yarrow256_is_seeded(struct yarrow256_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Reports whether the Yarrow-256 context is currently seeded and ready to generate cryptographically strong output. Non-zero indicates seeded, zero indicates not seeded.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via yarrow256_init.

functions.name: yarrow256_needed_sources
functions.signature: unsigned yarrow256_needed_sources(struct yarrow256_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Returns the number of additional entropy sources that must contribute before a slow reseed threshold is met. Useful for managing seeding strategy across multiple sources.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via yarrow256_init.

functions.name: yarrow256_fast_reseed
functions.signature: void yarrow256_fast_reseed(struct yarrow256_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Forces a fast reseed using the fast pool. Intended for situations where limited but sufficient entropy is available to refresh the generator state.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via yarrow256_init.
Should be called only when appropriate entropy has been accumulated in the fast pool; exact thresholds are managed internally and not specified in this header.

functions.name: yarrow256_slow_reseed
functions.signature: void yarrow256_slow_reseed(struct yarrow256_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Forces a slow reseed using both pools, typically requiring contributions from multiple sources. Used to perform a full-strength reseed.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via yarrow256_init.
Should be called only when sufficient entropy has been accumulated according to Yarrow policy; exact thresholds are internal and not specified in this header.

functions.name: yarrow_key_event_init
functions.signature: void yarrow_key_event_init(struct yarrow_key_event_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Initializes the key event entropy estimator context. Must be called before estimating entropy from key events.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a yarrow_key_event_ctx.
Must be called before yarrow_key_event_estimate.

functions.name: yarrow_key_event_estimate
functions.signature: unsigned yarrow_key_event_estimate(struct yarrow_key_event_ctx *ctx, unsigned key, unsigned time);
functions.description: Estimates the entropy contributed by a single key event, based on the key code and timing. Returns an entropy estimate (units likely bits) to be credited to the PRNG. Internal state tracks recent keys and timing to avoid overestimating.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via yarrow_key_event_init.
key should be the code of the key event; exact key range is not specified.
time is a timestamp or interval measurement used for entropy estimation; units and required monotonicity are not specified in this header (unknown).
May be called repeatedly for successive key events.
